46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis

Mendelian MONDO:0016674 Pathograph 49 Show in embeddings browser Disorder of sex development Gonadal development disorder

46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis (PGD) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder of testicular development with variable dysgenetic gonadal tissue and testicular hormone production. External genitalia range from female appearance to varying degrees of masculinization; Müllerian structures may be present or absent. Presentation may occur with atypical genitalia in infancy, pubertal delay or virilization, or impaired fertility. Some retained gonads support spontaneous puberty, but later hormone replacement may still be needed. Dysgenetic gonads can contain gonadoblastoma, germ cell neoplasia in situ, or invasive tumors. Genotype, gonadal function and anatomy, age, and the individual's goals inform care.

Definitions

1
46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis case definition
A 46,XY karyotype with evidence of incomplete or disordered testicular development, assessed through the genital phenotype, endocrine function, histology when available, and molecular findings. Atypical external genitalia are common but are not obligatory: the I-DSD study also included individuals with female external genitalia, absent uterus, and evidence of gonadal dysfunction. No single hormone value or histological pattern separates every partial and complete presentation.
CASE_DEFINITION This entry covers partial gonadal dysgenesis, including gene-specific syndromic forms. Complete gonadal dysgenesis, 45,X/46,XY mosaicism, ovotesticular DSD, testicular regression, androgen insensitivity, and steroid synthesis defects require distinction. A blood 46,XY result does not exclude low-level or tissue-confined sex-chromosome mosaicism.

"As 46,XY PGD is a heterogeneous disorder without clearly defined diagnostic criteria, we used the diagnostic criteria from a previous study which requires evidence of testicular dysgenesis, either in a biochemical test (e.g., low testosterone response after hCG stimulation, low AMH or inhibin..."

PMID:40208111 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Furthermore, standard karyotyping techniques may miss mosaicism such as 46,XY/45,X."
The registry authors explicitly identify a limitation of conventional karyotyping; a blood result does not exclude every mosaic cell line.

Inheritance

2
Autosomal dominant inheritance HP:0000006
Established heterozygous causes include NR5A1, MAP3K1, WT1 and DHX37. Transmission, penetrance and associated features are gene- and variant-dependent. An unaffected carrier parent can transmit a pathogenic allele; 50% transmission risk for an autosomal dominant allele is not equivalent to 50% risk of the same gonadal phenotype.
Autosomal dominant inheritance
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:33296094 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Segregation analysis across three generations showed incomplete penetrance (<50%) and phenotypic variability among the carriers of NR5A1 c.991-1G > C."
Directly documents dominant transmission with reduced penetrance in partial disease.
PMID:35290982 SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Other
"Inheritance occurs in a sex-limited, autosomal dominant fashion with virtually complete penetrance in 46,XY individuals."
Supports sex-limited dominant inheritance with gene-specific penetrance for MAP3K1.
Autosomal recessive inheritance HP:0000007
Biallelic DHH variants underlie a recessive form with sex-chromosome-dependent gonadal manifestations and possible peripheral neuropathy.
Autosomal recessive inheritance

PMID:11017805 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"a homozygous missense mutation (ATG-->ACG) at the initiating codon in exon 1 of the desert hedgehog (DHH) gene"
Homozygosity in the proband supports recessive inheritance.

Subtypes

6
gene
NR5A1/SF-1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
NR5A1 hgnc:7983 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in NR5A1 (hgnc:7983). hgnc:7983 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Autosomal dominant inheritance
Heterozygous NR5A1 variants, including truncating, missense and splice-site alleles, cause variable partial gonadal dysgenesis. NR5A1 was the most frequent molecular finding in the partial groups of the I-DSD registry. Spontaneous puberty and unaffected transmitting relatives are reported, but neither gonadal function nor fertility is guaranteed. Adrenal insufficiency is uncommon in the broader NR5A1-related DSD spectrum and should be evaluated when clinically indicated.

MAP3K1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
MAP3K1 hgnc:6848 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in MAP3K1 (hgnc:6848). hgnc:6848 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Autosomal dominant inheritance
Heterozygous MAP3K1 variants cause a sex-limited spectrum of partial and complete gonadal dysgenesis. A three-patient partial subgroup had clitoral hypertrophy with otherwise female external genitalia; other families include more masculinized partial presentations. Functional effects have been demonstrated for selected variants and should not be assumed for every rare missense allele. The review estimate of at least 4% concerns combined nonsyndromic partial and complete GD, not partial disease alone.

"the other three presented with partial gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by incomplete testicular development, resulting in clitoral hypertrophy with otherwise typical female external genitalia"
Directly documents the MAP3K1 partial phenotype and its genital pattern.
PMID:35290982 SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Other
"Pathogenic variants in the MAP3K1 gene are an important cause of 46,XY non-syndromic partial and complete gonadal dysgenesis, accounting for at least 4% of cases."

WT1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis (Denys-Drash/Frasier continuum)
WT1 hgnc:12796 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in WT1 (hgnc:12796). hgnc:12796 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Autosomal dominant inheritance
WT1-related testicular-development disorders may accompany glomerulopathy, steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and Wilms tumor predisposition, with variable combinations and timing. GeneReviews treats the historical Denys-Drash and Frasier labels as a phenotypic continuum. A reported whole-gene deletion caused severe partial dysgenesis and bilateral Wilms tumor; gonadal histology in infancy was described as suggestive of gonadoblastoma. Surveillance follows the molecular WT1 diagnosis even when renal findings are initially absent.

DHH-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis with minifascicular neuropathy
DHH hgnc:2865 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in DHH (hgnc:2865). hgnc:2865 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Autosomal recessive inheritance
Biallelic DHH variants can cause partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis. Reported partial cases include a dysgenetic testis with streak regions, abnormal Leydig-cell differentiation, and gonadal neoplasia. Peripheral neuropathy may accompany the gonadal disorder and can become apparent in adulthood; its absence in childhood does not exclude DHH-related disease.

DHX37-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
DHX37 hgnc:17210 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in DHX37 (hgnc:17210). hgnc:17210 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Autosomal dominant inheritance
Heterozygous DHX37 variants, notably recurrent p.Arg308Gln, are associated with partial gonadal dysgenesis and testicular regression. Some variants arise de novo and some are maternally inherited. Structural predictions and selected overexpression assays suggest altered protein function, but variant-dependent ATPase failure, defective ribosome production and the pathway to human gonadal dysgenesis have not been established. Co-occurring NR5A1 variants do not by themselves establish digenic inheritance.

molecular
Molecularly unresolved 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
A clinical diagnosis may remain without molecular confirmation. In the historical I-DSD registry, a likely gene or chromosome alteration was reported in 59.0% of screened PGDf individuals and 50.0% of screened PGDm individuals. Testing methods and variant classification varied; these selected-cohort results are not a fixed yield for current panels or genome sequencing.

Reports tested-subgroup yields; not a plateau or all-patient diagnostic sensitivity.

Discussions and Knowledge Gaps

4
What is the prospective, age-specific neoplasia risk in retained gonads in 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis, and how reliably can monitoring detect clinically significant lesions?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN gap_xy_pgd_gonad_retention_risk_benefit
Attached to
treatments#Individualized gonadal management (retention versus gonadectomy)
Registry estimates arise from selected histology subsets with different gonadectomy ages and inconsistent monitoring, not person-time follow-up of all retained gonads. Neither gonadal position nor hCG responsiveness is a validated rule for safe retention. Endocrine value and patient goals must be weighed against uncertain neoplasia risk.
Proposed experiments
Prospective registry follow-up of retained gonads in 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
exp_xy_pgd_retained_gonad_incidence
Follow retained gonads prospectively within a multinational DSD registry using protocolized imaging, tumor markers, and (where performed) biopsy, reporting neoplasia incidence per gonad-year stratified by gonadal position and hCG-stimulated testosterone response, rather than prevalence at gonadectomy.
Immunohistochemical germ-cell marker triage of gonadal biopsy material
exp_xy_pgd_ihc_germ_cell_marker_triage
Evaluate whether immunohistochemical germ-cell markers (for example OCT3/4, TSPY, SALL4) on gonadal biopsy material can stratify premalignant risk well enough to serve as a triage test for gonad retention versus removal.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:40208111 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"However, there was significant variation in monitoring practice amongst centers and only one third (n = 34/92) of individuals with PGDm had histology assessment."
Primary study identifies ascertainment and surveillance limitations.
Which unsolved partial-gonadal-dysgenesis cases are explained by noncoding variants, tissue-confined mosaicism, additional genes or true multilocus effects?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN gap_xy_pgd_molecular_yield
Attached to
diagnosis#Broad molecular testing including WT1
The I-DSD study identified a likely gene or chromosome alteration in 131/310 across complete and partial disease, but only 78.7% underwent screening and methods and variant classification varied. This is not evidence of a fixed diagnostic-yield plateau. SOX9 regulatory architecture is relevant broader DSD biology; the cited enhancer paper does not establish every deletion as partial disease. The NR5A1/DHX37 dual-variant cases include uncertain or likely-benign DHX37 findings and do not prove a multilocus explanation.
Proposed experiments
Genome sequencing with targeted gonadal-enhancer interrogation
exp_xy_pgd_enhancer_genome_sequencing
Apply genome sequencing to exome-negative partial-dysgenesis cases with explicit interrogation of known gonadal enhancer regions, including the testis-specific enhancers upstream of SOX9, to test whether non-coding regulatory variation explains part of the diagnostic gap.
Deep sequencing of gonadal tissue for gonad-confined mosaicism
exp_xy_pgd_gonadal_mosaicism_sequencing
Deep-sequence gonadal tissue obtained at gonadectomy alongside matched blood to test whether mosaic variants confined to the gonad account for cases undiagnosed on peripheral-blood testing.

PMID:37240737 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Secondly, patient 3 also carries a loss-of-function variant in NR5A1, which could fully explain the PGD phenotype, making the p.Val999Met variant a chance finding."

Do mouse Nr5a1 models faithfully reproduce the human NR5A1 gonadal phenotype, given that the same p.R92W substitution induces testicular development in human 46,XX gonads but produces no masculinization in XX mice?
HUMAN MODEL MISMATCH OPEN mismatch_xy_pgd_nr5a1_mouse_model_divergence
Attached to
pathophysiology#NR5A1 sequence alteration
The p.Arg92Trp comparison showed species differences, including absence of XX masculinization in mice despite human 46,XX testicular development. This is a caution about translating allele-specific sex-development models, not a claim that the mouse directly models every human PGD presentation.
Proposed experiments
Human gonadal organoid or iPSC titration of NR5A1 dosage
exp_xy_pgd_human_gonadal_organoid_nr5a1_dosage
Titrate NR5A1 dosage and introduce patient-specific alleles in human-derived gonadal somatic cell models (iPSC-derived or fetal gonadal organoid) to establish the human-specific dose-response threshold that separates partial from complete testis-determination failure, and compare it directly against the corresponding murine threshold.

Do established PGD-associated DHX37 alleles alter RNA-dependent ATPase activity, ribosome maturation, or another cell function in developing human gonadal cells?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN gap_xy_pgd_dhx37_biochemical_mechanism
Attached to
pathophysiology#DHX37 sequence alteration
The original study used structural modeling and expression/localization analysis. Later overexpression experiments measured abundance and selected signaling readouts, with unchanged p53 and no increase in apoptosis for p.Ser408Leu. The proposed ribosomopathy mechanism and the route from altered protein abundance to gonadal differentiation remain unproven.

PMID:37065748 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"Surprisingly, we did not see increases in the p53 protein and cell apoptosis by DHX37 mutation"

Pathophysiology

19
NR5A1 sequence alteration
Heterozygous pathogenic NR5A1 variants occur in partial gonadal dysgenesis. Early truncating alleles are predicted to reduce functional SF-1; other alleles have variant-specific effects. Nonsense-mediated decay and splice changes in the cited partial cases were predicted rather than directly measured.
NR5A1 hgnc:7983 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this gene This pathophysiological event involves NR5A1 (hgnc:7983). hgnc:7983 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee.
Downstream
Reduced SF-1 transcriptional activity Selected NR5A1 missense variants reduce a steroidogenic-promoter reporter in transfected cells; this does not establish the effect of every allele.
Incomplete testicular differentiation The genetic association establishes a developmental effect, but the causal fetal targets and thresholds vary and are not resolved for each allele.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:27463801 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"3 novel NR5A1 mutations were identified in 3 patients with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: p.Lys38* and p.Leu80Trpfs*8 lead to premature translation termination codons within the SF1 DNA-binding domain"
Directly documents loss-of-function NR5A1 variants in partial disease.
Reduced SF-1 transcriptional activity
p.Gly22Asp and p.Leu420Pro reduced Cyp11a1 promoter activation in kidney-derived tsa201 cells. This is an experimental readout of variant-dependent transcriptional function; it does not directly measure fetal Sertoli differentiation or all SF-1 target genes.

MAP3K1 sequence alteration
Heterozygous MAP3K1 variants are associated with partial and complete gonadal dysgenesis. Functional consequences below are allele- and assay-specific. The p.Arg186Gly family had severe 46,XY DSD with streak gonads or tumors; its cellular results inform a broader gene mechanism rather than prove the mechanism of every partial presentation.

Downstream
Enhanced MAP3K1-RHOA association Patient-derived and transfected-cell assays identify increased association for selected variants.
Reduced MAP3K1 ubiquitination The p.Arg186Gly construct shows reduced ubiquitination in HEK293T cells; mediation by increased RHOA binding remains an interpretation.
Increased MAP3K1 protein abundance The p.Arg186Gly construct produces more MAP3K1 protein in NT2/D1 and KGN cells.
Increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation Selected patient lymphoblastoid lines show altered ERK phosphorylation after serum refeeding.
Increased p38 phosphorylation The response occurs in selected patient lines and p.Arg186Gly overexpression models, with allele-dependent differences.
Increased beta-catenin-dependent transcription The p.Arg186Gly construct increases TCF/LEF reporter activity; intervening signaling was not dissected by epistasis.
Incomplete testicular differentiation Human pedigrees and cases support MAP3K1-related partial dysgenesis. The observed signaling changes propose, but do not experimentally reconstruct, the human fetal developmental route.

Selected MAP3K1 variants increase RHOA association in protein-interaction assays. The p.Arg186Gly study used both NanoBiT and co-immunoprecipitation. Stronger association alone does not prove that RHOA mediates all downstream signaling changes.

Biallelic DHH sequence alteration
Biallelic DHH variants are associated with gonadal dysgenesis and, in some patients, peripheral neuropathy. Initiating-codon translation failure and altered p.Arg124Gln ligand interactions were predicted; a universal complete loss of hedgehog signaling was not directly demonstrated in these cases.

Impaired Leydig-cell maturation
In one DHH p.Arg124Gln partial-dysgenesis gonad, CYP17A1-positive Leydig-like nodules were present but mature INSL3-positive Leydig cells were absent from tubular interstitium. This supports abnormal differentiation rather than absence of every steroidogenic cell. The finding is postnatal histology, not a direct fetal hormone measurement.

DHX37 sequence alteration
Recurrent heterozygous DHX37 variants, including p.Arg308Gln, occur in partial gonadal dysgenesis and testicular regression. Genetic association is established more strongly than the biochemical route. The proposed ribosomopathy mechanism must be distinguished from measured protein abundance and from uncertain variants.

Reduced DHX37 protein abundance
In transfected HEK293T cells, p.Arg308Gln and p.Arg671Thr showed lower DHX37 protein expression than wild type. A separate p.Ser408Leu Sertoli-cell assay also found lower transcript and protein abundance. p.Arg671Thr and p.Ser408Leu were listed as VUS in the later study table. These assays do not demonstrate variant-dependent ATPase failure, defective 18S rRNA maturation, or a causal connection from protein reduction to human gonadal dysgenesis.

WT1 sequence alteration
Pathogenic heterozygous WT1 variants can cause partial testicular dysgenesis within a variable renal and tumor-predisposition disorder. Effects differ between zinc-finger missense, splice, truncating and deletion alleles; a single generic haploinsufficiency mechanism cannot represent all of them.
WT1 hgnc:12796 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this gene This pathophysiological event involves WT1 (hgnc:12796). hgnc:12796 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee.
Downstream
Incomplete testicular differentiation The whole-gene deletion case directly documents severe partial dysgenesis; the disrupted fetal transcriptional program was not assayed.
Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome Pathogenic WT1 variants predispose to glomerular disease within WT1 disorder. This is restricted to the WT1-related subtype; intervening renal cellular mechanisms are not modeled here.
Nephroblastoma Wilms tumor occurred in the child with a WT1 whole-gene deletion and partial gonadal dysgenesis. This genotype-qualified link does not imply that every variant or affected person develops a tumor, or that the somatic initiating events were measured.

Incomplete testicular differentiation
The gonads can contain hypoplastic or disorganized testicular tissue, streak tissue and regressed regions in varying combinations. Sertoli, Leydig and germ-cell compartments need not be affected equally. Preserved testosterone, AMH or spontaneous puberty is compatible with partial dysgenesis and does not demonstrate normal fertility or absence of neoplasia.

Downstream
Gonadal dysgenesis Histology is a direct readout of abnormal tissue differentiation.
Reduced fetal AMH activity Müllerian retention in a subset is consistent with insufficient fetal AMH action; this is a developmental inference, not a fetal serum measurement.
Reduced fetal androgen activity Undervirilized external genital development is consistent with inadequate fetal testicular androgen activity; timing and output are inferred rather than measured.
Impaired spermatogenesis Abnormal tubular and germ-cell architecture plausibly contributes to the semen abnormalities observed in clinical follow-up; patient-specific mediation is not experimentally demonstrated.
Delayed gonadal germ-cell maturation OCT3/4-positive luminal cells in a MAP3K1-associated partial gonad demonstrate delayed maturation within dysgenetic tissue.
Decreased testicular size Underdeveloped testicular tissue is consistent with reduced volume in the reported NR5A1 case. The contribution of each histological compartment was not quantified.
Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism Primary gonadal dysfunction can reduce sex-steroid output and feedback, producing elevated gonadotropins with low testosterone in a subset; preserved androgen production in other partial cases remains compatible with dysgenesis.

Reduced fetal AMH activity
Insufficient anti-Müllerian hormone activity during the fetal differentiation window is a physiological interpretation of Müllerian retention in some partial cases. Other patients lack Müllerian structures, indicating that fetal AMH action may have been sufficient despite later gonadal dysfunction. Postnatal AMH measurements cannot retrospectively quantify the fetal exposure.

Reduced fetal androgen activity
Inadequate testicular androgen action during genital differentiation can produce undervirilized external genital anatomy. The degree and timing vary, and a female external phenotype is possible. Fetal steroid levels were not measured in the cited clinical cohorts.

Impaired spermatogenesis
Sperm production may be severely reduced or absent despite retained androgen production. Severe oligozoospermia and low motility occurred in the three semen-tested participants of one ten-patient follow-up cohort; azoospermia is documented in individual molecularly characterized partial cases.

Histopathology

2
Dysgenetic testis with hypoplastic seminiferous tubules
Partial disease can include dysgenetic testes, streak tissue or regressed gonads. Observed testicular abnormalities include reduced tubular diameter, thick basement membranes, irregular tubules, interstitial fibrosis, Sertoli-cell-only tubules and reduced germ cells. Histology contributes to diagnosis and neoplasia assessment but does not by itself classify every partial versus complete case; small biopsies can miss heterogeneous tissue.

Broader testicular-development guidance warns about sampling and potential harm.
Gonadoblastoma and germ cell neoplasia in situ in dysgenetic gonads
Gonadoblastoma and germ cell neoplasia in situ are distinct lesions reported in partial gonadal dysgenesis. DHH-related partial disease included GCNIS with incipient stromal invasion and gonadoblastoma. These are pathological findings, not an obligatory sequential progression in every gonad.

Medical Actions

Individualized gonadal management (retention versus gonadectomy)
Category: Therapeutic Action: orchiectomyNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is orchiectomy (NCIT:C15288). NCIT:C15288 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. Ontology label: Orchiectomy NCIT:C15288
Platform: Surgery
Discuss gonadal function, genotype, tissue location, available pathology, age, fertility potential and the individual's goals with an experienced DSD team. Nonfunctional high-risk dysgenetic gonads may warrant removal; potentially functional gonads may be retained after individualized discussion. Sex assignment and a preserved hCG response are not stand-alone indications for removal or retention. Surveillance options exist, but no strategy reliably excludes neoplasia; the registry percentages are selected histology prevalences rather than prospective risks for retained gonads.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS Gonadoblastoma — Removal of nonfunctional at-risk gonads may prevent gonadoblastoma; decisions remain individualized.

Individualized sex-steroid replacement
Category: Therapeutic Action: Hormone Replacement TherapyNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Hormone Replacement Therapy (NCIT:C15599). NCIT:C15599 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C15599

CHEBI:17347 is a therapeutic agent from Chemical Entities of Biological Interest.
Replace sex steroids when gonadal production is insufficient or after gonadectomy, according to the individual's desired pubertal development and clinical needs. Testosterone or 17-beta-estradiol is introduced gradually with monitoring; an endometrium-bearing uterus requires addition of progestogen after appropriate estrogen priming. Spontaneous pubertal onset does not guarantee completion. Endo-ERN guidance supports individualized induction around age 11 for girls with confirmed hypogonadism and around age 12 for boys at high risk without pubertal onset. These recommendations cover broader congenital hypogonadism; the guideline found no eligible comparative puberty-treatment studies specifically in males with PGD.
Mechanism Target:
BYPASSES Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism — Sex-steroid replacement addresses inadequate hormone production; it does not reverse the developmental lesion.

Continue endocrine review through puberty and adulthood, including clinical pubertal progression and age-appropriate gonadotropins and sex steroids. During induction, guideline follow-up is generally every three to six months, with assessment of growth, skeletal maturation, treatment response and adverse effects. Gene-specific genetic counseling
Category: Counseling / Informational Action: Genetic CounselingNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Genetic Counseling (NCIT:C15240). NCIT:C15240 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C15240
Use the established molecular diagnosis and parental testing for recurrence counseling. Autosomal dominant allele transmission is distinct from phenotypic penetrance; the <50% estimate in one NR5A1 family must not be generalized. Counsel NR5A1 relatives about variable gonadal function and primary ovarian insufficiency in some 46,XX carriers, WT1 relatives about renal/tumor surveillance, and DHH families about recessive inheritance and possible neuropathy. DHX37/NR5A1 dual findings that include a VUS or likely-benign allele do not establish digenic recurrence risk. Prenatal or preimplantation testing may be discussed when a familial pathogenic variant is known.

Diagnosis

5
Integrated clinical, endocrine, and karyotypic assessment
Integrate genital anatomy, gonadal palpability, family history, associated renal or neurological findings, karyotype, and age-appropriate endocrine testing. Assess FSH, LH, testosterone, AMH and often inhibin B in clinical context. A blood 46,XY result distinguishes many chromosomal diagnoses but cannot exclude low-level or gonad-confined mosaicism.
clinical assessment NCIT:C124351 NCI Thesaurus (NCIT)
Results: Atypical genitalia with a 46,XY karyotype and biochemical evidence of partial gonadal function.

hCG stimulation test for residual Leydig-cell function
hCG stimulation assesses residual testicular testosterone production and can complement the steroid profile. It is not a validated stand-alone predictor of spontaneous puberty: the small registry subgroup association had P=.087. Endocrine testing cannot identify which gonad functions or determine whether both do.

Progression

5
Fetal partial testis-determination phase
Age: embryonic and fetal development
The developmental disturbance begins during gonadal differentiation. Variable Sertoli- and Leydig-cell function can leave different internal and external genital configurations. Hormonal explanations of fetal anatomy are developmental inferences, not direct measurements of fetal hormone levels in the cited patients.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:28504475 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"partial gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by incomplete testicular development"
Directly supports incomplete (rather than absent) fetal testis development.
Neonatal and infantile atypical-genitalia recognition phase
Age: birth to infancy
Atypical genitalia frequently prompt recognition in infancy, but female external genitalia or later presentation with delayed puberty also occur. In the registry, atypical genitalia were the presenting feature in all PGDm and 62.1% of PGDf; these are ascertainment data, not a population phenotype frequency.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:40208111 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"due to atypical genitalia in all patients with PGDm and 62.1% in PGDf."
Registry presentation pattern with its sex-assignment groups.
Variable pubertal phase
Age: adolescence
Among 45 registry participants assigned male at age 13 years or older with at least one retained gonad, including nine reassigned from female before age 13, 36 had spontaneous pubertal onset. Ten of 33 with relevant treatment data later received testosterone; 16 of 27 with final-stage data reached Tanner G5 without hormone treatment. Among 26 assigned female at age 13 years or older with gonads and data, 11 developed virilization; four of these 11 also had gonadal tumors. These selected subsets do not predict an individual course.

Documents later supplementation despite spontaneous onset.
+ 3 more references
Long-term gonadal-tumor and fertility phase
Age: childhood through adulthood
Gonadal neoplasia can occur from childhood into adulthood. In the I-DSD histology-assessed subsets, combined malignancy or premalignancy occurred in 13/66 PGDf and 3/34 PGDm, compared with 28/83 CGD. The combined endpoint includes several tumor types and is neither a gonadoblastoma-specific frequency nor lifetime risk. Earlier gonadectomy, selection for histology and inconsistent surveillance limit comparisons. Semen testing in small partial-disease series found severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia even when androgen production was retained.

Adult gonadal-reserve decline phase
Age: adulthood
Endocrine function may decline after spontaneous puberty. In one ten-patient series, FSH was high or high-normal in 3/6 before puberty and 8/10 at final evaluation, while LH was high or high-normal in 5/10 at final assessment. Differing denominators prevent treating this as a uniform within-person decline. A p.Arg308Gln DHX37 case entered puberty spontaneously but required testosterone from age 17. Ongoing endocrine review is appropriate.

Prevalence

1
Worldwide
Unknown Unknown
A population prevalence specific to 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis is not established by these sources. The registry includes 210 selected partial cases. The Danish estimate of 1.5 per 100,000 live-born females concerns female-phenotype 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis across subtypes; it cannot be applied as a rate or lower bound for all partial disease.

🔀

Differential Diagnoses

6

Conditions with similar clinical presentations that must be differentiated from 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis:

46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis MONDO:0010765
Overlapping Features Typical complete gonadal dysgenesis presents with female external genitalia, Müllerian structures and gonadal failure. Streak gonads are common, but dysgenetic testicular tissue can also occur. Partial disease shows more variable anatomy and residual function. Classification integrates phenotype, hormones, histology and genetics; tumors can themselves produce sex steroids in either group.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:40208111 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Gonadal pre-/malignancy was found in 33.8% in CGD, 19.7% in PGDf, and 8.8% in PGDm."
A single cohort scoring both entities documents the tumor-risk gradient that separates them.
PMID:28504475 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Three of these individuals presented with complete gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by bilateral streak gonads with typical internal and external female genitalia, while the other three presented with partial gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by incomplete testicular development"
Directly contrasts the two phenotypes within one gene's spectrum — the cleanest available statement of the distinction.
45,X/46,XY mixed gonadal dysgenesis
Overlapping Features 45,X/46,XY mosaicism can resemble 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis. Gonadal asymmetry does not distinguish them, because a dysgenetic testis and contralateral streak tissue can also occur in 46,XY PGD. Adequate chromosome assessment is required, while low-level or tissue-confined mosaicism may escape a blood test.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:34070473 SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Other
"sex chromosome DSD (Klinefelter or Turner Syndrome, chimerism), XX-DSD, and 46 XY-DSD"
Supports separation of sex-chromosome DSD from 46,XY DSD; the asymmetric gonadal detail is clinical synthesis.
Partial androgen insensitivity syndrome
Overlapping Features Androgen insensitivity can produce overlapping external genital findings despite testicular differentiation and androgen production. AMH, testosterone and hCG responses may overlap with other DSD diagnoses, so no single normal hormone result excludes PGD or proves PAIS. Molecular findings and the overall anatomical/endocrine pattern guide differentiation.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:31745530 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"partially virilized 46,XY DSD (pvDSD) (n = 25), a group that included partial gonadal dysgenesis and those with a broad "partial androgen insensitivity syndrome" label."
Directly documents the clinical conflation of partial gonadal dysgenesis with PAIS, motivating molecular resolution.
46,XY androgen synthesis disorders
Overlapping Features Steroid synthesis or metabolism defects, including 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 and 5-alpha-reductase 2 deficiencies, can impair virilization despite testicular differentiation. Steroid profiles, selected stimulation testing and molecular results help distinguish these from gonadal dysgenesis; preserved AMH alone is not a definitive discriminator.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:34070473 SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Other
"46 XY-DSD (disorders of testicular development and disorders of androgen synthesis or action)"
Supports the mechanistic distinction within 46,XY DSD.
Ovotesticular disorder of sex development
Overlapping Features Ovotesticular DSD is defined by ovarian follicular and testicular tissue in the same individual. Histology can identify these components when tissue is clinically obtained, but sampling can miss heterogeneous tissue. This distinction does not justify routine whole-gonad removal solely for diagnosis.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:38206718 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"primary ovarian insufficiency and ovotesticular DSD in 46, XX individuals."
Establishes ovotesticular DSD as a distinct entity within the same gene's phenotypic spectrum; the histological criterion is clinical synthesis.
Testicular regression syndrome
Overlapping Features Testicular regression reflects loss of previously differentiated testicular tissue rather than failure to differentiate it. The distinction can be genuinely difficult, and DHX37 variants are found in both cohorts, so the two are best regarded as adjacent points on a spectrum of testis-development failure.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:37240737 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"including complete and partial GD (PGD) and testicular regression syndrome (TRS)"
Places testicular regression syndrome alongside partial dysgenesis in the same disease group with shared genetic causes.

Animal Models

1
Sox9-Cre conditional Nr5a1 knockout mice
Conditional Nr5a1 loss in the Sox9 lineage reduced AMH-positive cells, impaired Sertoli differentiation and permitted ectopic FOXL2-positive cells. The reported postnatal spectrum included partial and complete gonadal sex reversal.

name: 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
creation_date: '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z'
category: Mendelian
description: >-
  46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis (PGD) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder of testicular development
  with variable dysgenetic gonadal tissue and testicular hormone production. External genitalia range
  from female appearance to varying degrees of masculinization; Müllerian structures may be present or
  absent. Presentation may occur with atypical genitalia in infancy, pubertal delay or virilization, or
  impaired fertility. Some retained gonads support spontaneous puberty, but later hormone replacement
  may still be needed. Dysgenetic gonads can contain gonadoblastoma, germ cell neoplasia in situ, or invasive
  tumors. Genotype, gonadal function and anatomy, age, and the individual's goals inform care.

    the genital phenotype, endocrine function, histology when available, and molecular findings. Atypical
    external genitalia are common but are not obligatory: the I-DSD study also included individuals with
    female external genitalia, absent uterus, and evidence of gonadal dysfunction. No single hormone value
    or histological pattern separates every partial and complete presentation.

    dysgenesis, 45,X/46,XY mosaicism, ovotesticular DSD, testicular regression, androgen insensitivity,
    and steroid synthesis defects require distinction. A blood 46,XY result does not exclude low-level
    or tissue-confined sex-chromosome mosaicism.

    as suggestive of gonadoblastoma. Surveillance follows the molecular WT1 diagnosis even when renal
    findings are initially absent.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25613702
    reference_title: >-
      WT1 deletion leading to severe 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis, Wilms tumor and gonadoblastoma: case report.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We describe a newborn with 46,XY severe partial gonadal dysgenesis
    explanation: Directly documents WT1-associated partial gonadal dysgenesis.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK556455/
    reference_title: WT1 Disorder - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      WT1 disorder is characterized by congenital /infantile or childhood onset of steroid-resistant nephrotic
      syndrome (SRNS), a progressive glomerulopathy that does not respond to standard steroid therapy.
    explanation: Current full GeneReviews clinical baseline for WT1-associated manifestations.
- name: DHH-related PGD
  display_name: DHH-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis with minifascicular neuropathy
  classification: gene
  genes:
  - preferred_term: DHH
    term:
      id: hgnc:2865
      label: DHH
  inheritance:
  - name: Autosomal recessive inheritance
    inheritance_term:
      preferred_term: Autosomal recessive inheritance
      term:
        id: HP:0000007
        label: Autosomal recessive inheritance
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:11017805
      reference_title: >-
        A novel mutation of desert hedgehog in a patient with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis accompanied
        by minifascicular neuropathy.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        We found, in the patient, a homozygous missense mutation (ATG-->ACG) at the initiating codon in
        exon 1 of the desert hedgehog (DHH) gene
      explanation: Homozygosity with a heterozygous carrier father supports recessive inheritance.
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  description: >-
    Biallelic DHH variants can cause partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis. Reported partial cases include
    a dysgenetic testis with streak regions, abnormal Leydig-cell differentiation, and gonadal neoplasia.
    Peripheral neuropathy may accompany the gonadal disorder and can become apparent in adulthood; its
    absence in childhood does not exclude DHH-related disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11017805
    reference_title: >-
      A novel mutation of desert hedgehog in a patient with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis accompanied
      by minifascicular neuropathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: mutation of the DHH gene may cause 46, XY PGD associated with minifascicular neuropathy.
    explanation: Directly links biallelic DHH defects to partial disease with neuropathy.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:25927242
    reference_title: >-
      46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis due to a Homozygous Mutation in Desert Hedgehog (DHH) Identified by Exome
      Sequencing.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We identified a novel homozygous R124Q mutation in the desert hedgehog gene (DHH)
    explanation: An independent consanguineous family, so the subtype no longer rests on a single 2000 case report.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:25927242
    reference_title: >-
      46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis due to a Homozygous Mutation in Desert Hedgehog (DHH) Identified by Exome
      Sequencing.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Mutations in DHH play a role in 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis and are associated with seminoma formation
      and a neuropathy with minifascicle formation.
    explanation: Confirms the gonad-plus-neuropathy pairing and adds seminoma risk to this subtype's profile.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: DHX37-related PGD
  display_name: DHX37-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
  classification: gene
  genes:
  - preferred_term: DHX37
    term:
      id: hgnc:17210
      label: DHX37
  inheritance:
  - name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
    inheritance_term:
      preferred_term: Autosomal dominant inheritance
      term:
        id: HP:0000006
        label: Autosomal dominant inheritance
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37240737
      reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: In DHX37, the variant p.(Arg308Gln), recurrent associated with DSD, was identified in one patient
      explanation: >-
        Documents a heterozygous recurrent DHX37 allele in partial disease. The unrelated dual-variant
        cases do not establish digenic inheritance.
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  description: >-
    Heterozygous DHX37 variants, notably recurrent p.Arg308Gln, are associated with partial gonadal dysgenesis
    and testicular regression. Some variants arise de novo and some are maternally inherited. Structural
    predictions and selected overexpression assays suggest altered protein function, but variant-dependent
    ATPase failure, defective ribosome production and the pathway to human gonadal dysgenesis have not
    been established. Co-occurring NR5A1 variants do not by themselves establish digenic inheritance.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Recent studies have identified variants in DHX37, a gene encoding a putative RNA helicase essential
      in ribosome biogenesis and previously associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, as a cause of
      PGD and TRS.
    explanation: Directly establishes DHX37 as a cause of partial gonadal dysgenesis.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:31337883
    reference_title: >-
      Pathogenic variants in the DEAH-box RNA helicase DHX37 are a frequent cause of 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis
      and 46,XY testicular regression syndrome.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      DHX37 pathogenic variants are a new cause of an autosomal dominant form of 46,XY DSD, including
      gonadal dysgenesis and TRS, showing that these conditions are part of a clinical spectrum.
    explanation: >-
      The primary discovery cohort establishes autosomal dominant inheritance and places gonadal dysgenesis
      and testicular regression on one spectrum.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: Molecularly unresolved PGD
  display_name: Molecularly unresolved 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
  classification: molecular
  description: >-
    A clinical diagnosis may remain without molecular confirmation. In the historical I-DSD registry,
    a likely gene or chromosome alteration was reported in 59.0% of screened PGDf individuals and 50.0%
    of screened PGDm individuals. Testing methods and variant classification varied; these selected-cohort
    results are not a fixed yield for current panels or genome sequencing.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Of those who underwent screening, 48.3% of individuals with CGD, 59.0% with PGDf, and 50.0% with
      PGDm had a gene or chromosome alteration identified.
    explanation: Reports tested-subgroup yields; not a plateau or all-patient diagnostic sensitivity.
prevalence:
- population: Worldwide
  measure_type: UNKNOWN
  prevalence_class: UNKNOWN
  notes: >-
    A population prevalence specific to 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis is not established by these sources.
    The registry includes 210 selected partial cases. The Danish estimate of 1.5 per 100,000 live-born
    females concerns female-phenotype 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis across subtypes; it cannot be applied as
    a rate or lower bound for all partial disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Patients with 46,XY GD were identified from the I-DSD Registry
    explanation: Documents referral-registry ascertainment, which does not estimate population prevalence.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:27603905
    reference_title: >-
      Incidence, Prevalence, Diagnostic Delay, and Clinical Presentation of Female 46,XY Disorders of
      Sex Development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The prevalence of 46,XY females was 6.4 per 100 000 live born females, and for AIS and gonadal dysgenesis,
      it was 4.1 and 1.5 per 100 000, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      Female-phenotype gonadal dysgenesis estimate across subtypes; explicitly not adopted as the partial-disease
      prevalence.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
inheritance:
- name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Autosomal dominant inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0000006
      label: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  description: >-
    Established heterozygous causes include NR5A1, MAP3K1, WT1 and DHX37. Transmission, penetrance and
    associated features are gene- and variant-dependent. An unaffected carrier parent can transmit a pathogenic
    allele; 50% transmission risk for an autosomal dominant allele is not equivalent to 50% risk of the
    same gonadal phenotype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33296094
    reference_title: >-
      NR5A1 c.991-1G > C splice-site variant causes familial 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis with incomplete
      penetrance.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Segregation analysis across three generations showed incomplete penetrance (<50%) and phenotypic
      variability among the carriers of NR5A1 c.991-1G > C.
    explanation: Directly documents dominant transmission with reduced penetrance in partial disease.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:35290982
    reference_title: 'Pathogenic Variants in MAP3K1 Cause 46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis: A Review.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Inheritance occurs in a sex-limited, autosomal dominant fashion with virtually complete penetrance
      in 46,XY individuals.
    explanation: Supports sex-limited dominant inheritance with gene-specific penetrance for MAP3K1.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
- name: Autosomal recessive inheritance
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Autosomal recessive inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0000007
      label: Autosomal recessive inheritance
  description: >-
    Biallelic DHH variants underlie a recessive form with sex-chromosome-dependent gonadal manifestations
    and possible peripheral neuropathy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11017805
    reference_title: >-
      A novel mutation of desert hedgehog in a patient with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis accompanied
      by minifascicular neuropathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      a homozygous missense mutation (ATG-->ACG) at the initiating codon in exon 1 of the desert hedgehog
      (DHH) gene
    explanation: Homozygosity in the proband supports recessive inheritance.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
progression:
- phase: Fetal partial testis-determination phase
  age_range: embryonic and fetal development
  notes: >-
    The developmental disturbance begins during gonadal differentiation. Variable Sertoli- and Leydig-cell
    function can leave different internal and external genital configurations. Hormonal explanations of
    fetal anatomy are developmental inferences, not direct measurements of fetal hormone levels in the
    cited patients.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28504475
    reference_title: 'MAP3K1-related gonadal dysgenesis: Six new cases and review of the literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: partial gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by incomplete testicular development
    explanation: Directly supports incomplete (rather than absent) fetal testis development.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- phase: Neonatal and infantile atypical-genitalia recognition phase
  age_range: birth to infancy
  notes: >-
    Atypical genitalia frequently prompt recognition in infancy, but female external genitalia or later
    presentation with delayed puberty also occur. In the registry, atypical genitalia were the presenting
    feature in all PGDm and 62.1% of PGDf; these are ascertainment data, not a population phenotype frequency.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: due to atypical genitalia in all patients with PGDm and 62.1% in PGDf.
    explanation: Registry presentation pattern with its sex-assignment groups.
- phase: Variable pubertal phase
  age_range: adolescence
  notes: >-
    Among 45 registry participants assigned male at age 13 years or older with at least one retained gonad,
    including nine reassigned from female before age 13, 36 had spontaneous pubertal onset. Ten of 33
    with relevant treatment data later received testosterone; 16 of 27 with final-stage data reached Tanner
    G5 without hormone treatment. Among 26 assigned female at age 13 years or older with gonads and data,
    11 developed virilization; four of these 11 also had gonadal tumors. These selected subsets do not
    predict an individual course.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Information on puberty was available in 45 individuals with PGD who assigned male at age ≥13 years,
      including 9 individuals reassigned from female to male before age 13 years, with at least 1 retained
      gonad (bilateral gonads n = 37, unilateral n = 8).
    explanation: Defines the retained-gonad puberty denominator and reassigned participants.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Spontaneous onset of puberty (Tanner stage G2 or testis volume ≥4 mL) occurred in 80.0% (n = 36/45)
    explanation: Supplies observed spontaneous onset.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Of these, 30.3% (n = 10/33) were treated with testosterone to complete puberty
    explanation: Documents later supplementation despite spontaneous onset.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: In puberty completion assessment, 59.3% (n = 16/27) achieved Tanner G5 without hormone treatment
    explanation: Defines the completion denominator.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Of individuals with PGD assigned female at age ≥13 years with at least 1 gonad (n = 18/22 individuals
      with intra-abdominal or impalpable gonad, n = 4/22 uni-/bilateral inguinal gonad) 42.3% (n = 11/26)
      developed features of virilization (hirsutism n = 5, clitoral enlargement n = 7) (Table 5)
    explanation: Reports the female-assigned retained-gonad subgroup, not all PGDf.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: 36.4% (n = 4/11) of virilization associated with tumor (gonadoblastoma, dysgerminoma, seminoma)
    explanation: Table 5 shows tumor association in four of the eleven virilizing PGDf individuals.
- phase: Long-term gonadal-tumor and fertility phase
  age_range: childhood through adulthood
  notes: >-
    Gonadal neoplasia can occur from childhood into adulthood. In the I-DSD histology-assessed subsets,
    combined malignancy or premalignancy occurred in 13/66 PGDf and 3/34 PGDm, compared with 28/83 CGD.
    The combined endpoint includes several tumor types and is neither a gonadoblastoma-specific frequency
    nor lifetime risk. Earlier gonadectomy, selection for histology and inconsistent surveillance limit
    comparisons. Semen testing in small partial-disease series found severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia
    even when androgen production was retained.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Gonadal malignancy or premalignancy (germ cell neoplasia in situ) was reported in 33.7% (n = 28/83;
      18.1% unilateral, 15.7% bilateral) in CGD, 19.7% (n = 13/66; 4.5% unilateral, 15.2% bilateral) in
      PGDf, and 8.8% (n = 3/34; 5.9% unilateral, 2.9% bilateral) in PGDm (CGD vs PGDf, P = .066; CGD vs
      PGDm, P = .005).
    explanation: Observed histology-subset denominators and combined endpoint.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      However, there was significant variation in monitoring practice amongst centers and only one third
      (n = 34/92) of individuals with PGDm had histology assessment.
    explanation: Limits interpretation of low observed PGDm tumor prevalence.
  - reference: PMID:25580123
    reference_title: Long-Term Follow-Up of Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis Reared as Males.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Three patients had a sperm count; all had severe oligozoospermia and low motility, and two had also
      abnormal semen viscosity.
    explanation: Direct limited-cohort semen findings.
- phase: Adult gonadal-reserve decline phase
  age_range: adulthood
  notes: >-
    Endocrine function may decline after spontaneous puberty. In one ten-patient series, FSH was high
    or high-normal in 3/6 before puberty and 8/10 at final evaluation, while LH was high or high-normal
    in 5/10 at final assessment. Differing denominators prevent treating this as a uniform within-person
    decline. A p.Arg308Gln DHX37 case entered puberty spontaneously but required testosterone from age
    17. Ongoing endocrine review is appropriate.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25580123
    reference_title: Long-Term Follow-Up of Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis Reared as Males.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At the end of the prepubertal period, FSH was high or high-normal in 3/6 patients; LH was normal
      in all. At the last evaluation, FSH was high or high-normal in 8/10; LH was high or high-normal
      in 5/10
    explanation: >-
      Consistent with rising gonadotropins over follow-up, but limited by n=10 single-centre, and the
      3/6 and 8/10 fractions have different denominators, so this is not a within-patient longitudinal
      comparison.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      The patient developed normal puberty at 12 years old but presented with low testosterone levels
      at 17 years old.
    explanation: Individual longitudinal observation of later testosterone deficiency.
pathophysiology:
- name: NR5A1 sequence alteration
  role: trigger
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    Heterozygous pathogenic NR5A1 variants occur in partial gonadal dysgenesis. Early truncating alleles
    are predicted to reduce functional SF-1; other alleles have variant-specific effects. Nonsense-mediated
    decay and splice changes in the cited partial cases were predicted rather than directly measured.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27463801
    reference_title: >-
      NR5A1 Loss-of-Function Mutations Lead to 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis Phenotype: Report of Three
      Novel Mutations.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      3 novel NR5A1 mutations were identified in 3 patients with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: p.Lys38*
      and p.Leu80Trpfs*8 lead to premature translation termination codons within the SF1 DNA-binding domain
    explanation: Directly documents loss-of-function NR5A1 variants in partial disease.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NR5A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:7983
      label: NR5A1
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced SF-1 transcriptional activity
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Selected NR5A1 missense variants reduce a steroidogenic-promoter reporter in transfected cells;
      this does not establish the effect of every allele.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:31745530
      reference_title: >-
        Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals Novel Genetic Variants (SRY, DMRT1, NR5A1, DHH, DHX37) in Adults
        With 46,XY DSD.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        Transient transfection assays showing activation of a Cyp11a1 promoter by WT SF-1 and impaired
        transcriptional activity by the p.G22D and p.L420P mutants.
      explanation: >-
        Cyp11a1 reporter in tsa201 kidney-derived cells; the clinical cohort used a broader partially
        virilized DSD category.
  - target: Incomplete testicular differentiation
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      The genetic association establishes a developmental effect, but the causal fetal targets and thresholds
      vary and are not resolved for each allele.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:27463801
      reference_title: >-
        NR5A1 Loss-of-Function Mutations Lead to 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis Phenotype: Report of
        Three Novel Mutations.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        3 novel NR5A1 mutations were identified in 3 patients with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: p.Lys38*
        and p.Leu80Trpfs*8 lead to premature translation termination codons within the SF1 DNA-binding
        domain
      explanation: Directly documents loss-of-function NR5A1 variants in partial disease.
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: Reduced SF-1 transcriptional activity
  role: intermediate
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    p.Gly22Asp and p.Leu420Pro reduced Cyp11a1 promoter activation in kidney-derived tsa201 cells. This
    is an experimental readout of variant-dependent transcriptional function; it does not directly measure
    fetal Sertoli differentiation or all SF-1 target genes.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31745530
    reference_title: >-
      Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals Novel Genetic Variants (SRY, DMRT1, NR5A1, DHH, DHX37) in Adults
      With 46,XY DSD.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Transient transfection assays showing activation of a Cyp11a1 promoter by WT SF-1 and impaired transcriptional
      activity by the p.G22D and p.L420P mutants.
    explanation: >-
      Cyp11a1 reporter in tsa201 kidney-derived cells; the clinical cohort used a broader partially virilized
      DSD category.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NR5A1
    term:
      id: hgnc:7983
      label: NR5A1
- name: MAP3K1 sequence alteration
  role: trigger
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    Heterozygous MAP3K1 variants are associated with partial and complete gonadal dysgenesis. Functional
    consequences below are allele- and assay-specific. The p.Arg186Gly family had severe 46,XY DSD with
    streak gonads or tumors; its cellular results inform a broader gene mechanism rather than prove the
    mechanism of every partial presentation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21129722
    reference_title: >-
      Mutations in MAP3K1 cause 46,XY disorders of sex development and implicate a common signal transduction
      pathway in human testis determination.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      mutations in MAP3K1 that result in 46,XY DSD with partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis implicate
      this pathway in normal human sex determination.
    explanation: Directly names partial gonadal dysgenesis as a MAP3K1 outcome.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MAP3K1
    term:
      id: hgnc:6848
      label: MAP3K1
  downstream:
  - target: Enhanced MAP3K1-RHOA association
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: Patient-derived and transfected-cell assays identify increased association for selected variants.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:21129722
      reference_title: >-
        Mutations in MAP3K1 cause 46,XY disorders of sex development and implicate a common signal transduction
        pathway in human testis determination.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        these mutations altered the phosphorylation of the downstream targets, p38 and ERK1/2, and enhanced
        binding of RHOA to the MAP3K1 complex.
      explanation: >-
        Patient lymphoblastoid-cell assays support altered MAPK phosphorylation and RHOA association;
        p38 effects differed among alleles.
    - reference: PMID:35309143
      reference_title: >-
        MAP3K1 Variant Causes Hyperactivation of Wnt4/β-Catenin/FOXL2 Signaling Contributing to 46,XY
        Disorders/Differences of Sex Development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        Our Co-IP assay confirmed that the binding capacity of MAP3K1R186G to RhoA was 2.57 times that
        of the wild-type protein (Figures 5A,A'), and the ubiquitination degree of the wild-type MAP3K1
        protein was 3.6-fold that of the MAP3K1R186G variant (Figures 5B,B').
      explanation: >-
        Selected p.Arg186Gly variant in HEK293T cells; binding and ubiquitination measurements, not gonadal

- name: Biallelic DHH sequence alteration
  role: trigger
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    Biallelic DHH variants are associated with gonadal dysgenesis and, in some patients, peripheral neuropathy.
    Initiating-codon translation failure and altered p.Arg124Gln ligand interactions were predicted; a
    universal complete loss of hedgehog signaling was not directly demonstrated in these cases.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11017805
    reference_title: >-
      A novel mutation of desert hedgehog in a patient with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis accompanied
      by minifascicular neuropathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      a homozygous missense mutation (ATG-->ACG) at the initiating codon in exon 1 of the desert hedgehog
      (DHH) gene, which predicts a failure of translation of the gene.
    explanation: Directly documents a causal biallelic DHH lesion in partial disease.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:25927242
    reference_title: >-
      46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis due to a Homozygous Mutation in Desert Hedgehog (DHH) Identified by Exome
      Sequencing.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      The gonads of one patient showed partial gonadal dysgenesis with loss of Leydig cells in tubular
      areas with seminoma in situ and a hyperplasia of Leydig cell-like cells expressing CYP17A1 in more
      dysgenetic parts of the gonad.
    explanation: >-
      Human gonadal pathology with biallelic DHH p.Arg124Gln; the molecular signaling defect was not directly
      assayed.

    term:
      id: hgnc:2865

- name: Delayed gonadal germ-cell maturation
  role: intermediate
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    In a partial gonad with a MAP3K1 defect, luminal OCT3/4-positive cells were interpreted as delayed
    maturation and peripheral cells as preneoplastic. Delayed maturation is not itself synonymous with
    neoplasia. The molecular steps linking a dysgenetic Y-bearing gonadal environment to a tumor remain
    incompletely defined.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      OCT3/4 staining (B.2) shows peripheral preneoplastic cells (gray arrow) and luminal OCT3/4-positive
      delayed maturation in white arrow.
    explanation: Human histology differentiates maturation delay from preneoplastic location.
  notes: >-
    No maturation-delay-to-neoplasia edge is asserted. The cited cross-sectional histology distinguishes
    luminal delayed maturation from peripheral preneoplastic cells; it does not demonstrate progression
    of the former population to gonadoblastoma or GCNIS.

biochemical:
- name: Follicle-stimulating hormone
  presence: INCREASED
  context: >-
    FSH elevation may indicate impaired Sertoli/tubular feedback despite preserved testosterone. Interpretation
    depends on developmental stage and the assay. The registry reported elevated FSH at age 0-6 months
    in 19/28 PGDf and 22/34 PGDm; normal values also occurred.
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: Follicle stimulating hormone
    term:
      id: CHEBI:81569
      label: Follicle stimulating hormone
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      | FSH elevated: 0-6 mo a | 100% (n = 6/6) | 67.9% (n = 19/28) | 64.7% (n = 22/34) | CGD vs PGDf
      ns CGD vs PGDm ns PGDf vs PGDm ns |
    explanation: Age- and group-specific FSH measurements; not a uniform finding.
  readouts:
  - target: Incomplete testicular differentiation
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: POSITIVE
    endpoint_context: DIAGNOSTIC
    interpretation: >-
      Elevated FSH may reflect the tubular/Sertoli component of current gonadal dysfunction; it is not
      a direct measure of androgen deficiency.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40208111
      reference_title: >-
        Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        | FSH elevated: 0-6 mo a | 100% (n = 6/6) | 67.9% (n = 19/28) | 64.7% (n = 22/34) | CGD vs PGDf
        ns CGD vs PGDm ns PGDf vs PGDm ns |
      explanation: Age- and group-specific FSH measurements; not a uniform finding.
- name: Testosterone response to hCG stimulation
  presence: ABNORMAL
  context: >-
    The hCG test assesses residual testosterone production. A greater than twofold rise was observed in
    15/17 participants with spontaneous puberty versus 1/3 with induced puberty, P=.087, in the small
    tested registry subset. This nonsignificant association is not a validated prediction rule or treatment
    threshold. A response does not localize function to one or both gonads.
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: testosterone
    term:
      id: CHEBI:17347
      label: testosterone
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Also, a higher proportion of individuals in the spontaneous puberty group had a testosterone response
      to hCG more than double the basal level (88%; n = 15/17, vs 33%; n = 1/3, P = .087).
    explanation: The full-text counts and P=.087 qualify the stronger abstract wording; not validated prediction.
  readouts:
  - target: Incomplete testicular differentiation
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: NEGATIVE
    endpoint_context: DIAGNOSTIC
    interpretation: >-
      A blunted hCG testosterone response may support impaired gonadal function in context; an adequate
      response does not exclude PGD or validate a puberty forecast.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40208111
      reference_title: >-
        Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        testosterone levels after human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) stimulation test less than twice
        the basal value
      explanation: One study diagnostic criterion, not a universally validated cutoff.
- name: Anti-Müllerian hormone
  presence: DECREASED
  context: >-
    AMH provides an age- and assay-dependent assessment of current Sertoli-cell function. It was low in
    12/25 PGDf and 18/31 PGDm in the registry, with normal values in the remaining measured individuals.
    Postnatal serum AMH does not directly measure fetal exposure and is not a stand-alone partial-versus-complete
    discriminator.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      | Low | 95.7% (n = 22/23) | 48.0% (n = 12/25) | 58.1% (n = 18/31) | CGD vs PGDf .0003 CGD vs PGDm
      .002 PGDf vs PGDm ns |
    explanation: 'AMH row in Table 3: CGD, PGDf, PGDm; age-specific reference ranges and small tested subsets.'
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      For AMH analysis, each institution used either ELISA or chemiluminescence immunoassay and the age-specific
      male reference was used for assessment (Beckman Coulter Cat# A73818, RRID:AB_3674123; Beckman Coulter
      Cat# B13127, RRID:AB_2892998; Roche Cat# 06331076, RRID:AB_2895131).
    explanation: Specifies assay and age-dependent interpretation.
- name: Inhibin B
  presence: DECREASED
  context: >-
    Inhibin B was low in 8/12 PGDf and 9/13 PGDm individuals with measurements. It complements AMH and
    gonadotropins in assessing current testicular function. These data do not establish a disease-specific
    cutoff or prove that inhibin B separates all DSD categories.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      | Low | 100% (n = 20/20) | 66.7% (n = 8/12) | 69.2% (n = 9/13) | CGD vs PGDf .014 CGD vs PGDm .016
      PGDf vs PGDm ns |
    explanation: 'Inhibin B row in Table 3: CGD, PGDf, PGDm; limited tested subsets.'

  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE

  - reference: PMID:27463801
    reference_title: >-

      Novel Mutations.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

      3 novel NR5A1 mutations were identified in 3 patients with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: p.Lys38*
      and p.Leu80Trpfs*8 lead to premature translation termination codons within the SF1 DNA-binding domain
    explanation: Directly documents loss-of-function NR5A1 variants in partial disease.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: with common gene defects in SRY and WT1 in CGD and NR5A1 in PGD.
    explanation: Establishes NR5A1 as the characteristic partial-disease gene.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: url:https://dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/316657/5/Laan_Maintext_final.pdf
    reference_title: https://dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/316657/5/Laan_Maintext_final.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Segregation analysis across three generations showed incomplete penetrance (<50%) and phenotypic
      variability among the carriers of NR5A1 c.991-1G>C.
    explanation: Family-specific penetrance, not a general NR5A1 penetrance estimate.
  notes: >-
    Reported variants include early truncations p.Lys38* and p.Leu80Trpfs*8, missense alleles and c.991-1G>C.
    The latter segregated with incomplete penetrance in one extended family; the reported <50% is family-
    and allele-specific, not a general counseling estimate. Its splice effect was predicted, not measured
    in patient RNA. NR5A1-related DSD may rarely accompany adrenal insufficiency; relatives with a 46,XX
    complement can have primary ovarian insufficiency.
