  gene_term:
    preferred_term: DHX37
    term:
      id: hgnc:17210
      label: DHX37
  association: >-
    Heterozygous variants associated with partial gonadal dysgenesis and testicular regression, including
    recurrent p.Arg308Gln
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  variant_origin: GERMLINE
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In DHX37, the variant p.(Arg308Gln), recurrent associated with DSD, was identified in one patient
    explanation: Directly documents the recurrent DHX37 allele in a partial-disease cohort.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Secondly, patient 3 also carries a loss-of-function variant in NR5A1, which could fully explain
      the PGD phenotype, making the p.Val999Met variant a chance finding.
    explanation: Authors explicitly acknowledge NR5A1 sufficiency and a possible chance DHX37 finding.
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      | 2 | DHX37 | c.1399C>G/ p.Leu467Val | rs149331610 | 0.0002952 1 /38 | VUS | 22.2 | Disease causing
      | Probably damaging | Deleterious | Maternal |
    explanation: Table 2 classification is uncertain despite damaging prediction scores.
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      | 3 | DHX37 | c.2995G>A/ p.Val999Met | rs148710712 | 0.002316 2 /54 | Likely Benign | 24.8 | Disease
      causing | Probably damaging | Deleterious | Paternal |
    explanation: >-
      Table 2 classifies Val999Met as likely benign; do not convert in-silico predictions into proven
      causality.
  notes: >-
    The 2023 dual-variant cases carried pathogenic NR5A1 variants with DHX37 p.Leu467Val classified as
    VUS or p.Val999Met classified as likely benign in Table 2. NR5A1 could explain their phenotypes; digenic
    causation remains unproven. For p.Arg308Gln, the original structural study predicted altered RNA interaction
    rather than measuring ATPase activity. Later overexpression assays found reduced protein abundance
    for selected variants, without demonstrating defective ribosome output.
- name: DHH
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: DHH
    term:
      id: hgnc:2865
      label: DHH
  association: >-
    Biallelic variants associated with partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis and possible peripheral
    neuropathy
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  variant_origin: GERMLINE
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11017805
    reference_title: >-
      A novel mutation of desert hedgehog in a patient with 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis accompanied
      by minifascicular neuropathy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      a homozygous missense mutation (ATG-->ACG) at the initiating codon in exon 1 of the desert hedgehog
      (DHH) gene, which predicts a failure of translation of the gene.
    explanation: Directly documents a causal biallelic DHH lesion in partial disease.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:25927242
    reference_title: >-
      46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis due to a Homozygous Mutation in Desert Hedgehog (DHH) Identified by Exome
      Sequencing.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      The gonads of one patient showed partial gonadal dysgenesis with loss of Leydig cells in tubular
      areas with seminoma in situ and a hyperplasia of Leydig cell-like cells expressing CYP17A1 in more
      dysgenetic parts of the gonad.
    explanation: Direct partial phenotype and Leydig-cell finding.
  notes: >-
    The initiating-codon variant was predicted to impair translation. Homozygous p.Arg124Gln was identified
    in two affected sisters; structural modeling predicted altered interaction with several signaling
    partners, without a direct ligand-function assay. In one sister, partial dysgenesis with loss of mature
    Leydig-cell staining was documented.
- name: ZFPM2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ZFPM2
    term:
      id: hgnc:16700
      label: ZFPM2
  association: Candidate association requiring variant-specific reassessment
  relationship_type: UNKNOWN
  variant_origin: GERMLINE
  notes: >-
    The initial report included a partial-dysgenesis patient with p.Met544Ile homozygosity and heterozygous
    p.Arg260Gln, and a complete-dysgenesis patient with p.Ser402Arg. Later work classified p.Met544Ile
    as benign and found normal activity for the tested ZFPM2 variants. This does not refute all possible
    ZFPM2 involvement, but does not justify a confirmed causal PGD subtype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24549039
    reference_title: Mutations in the FOG2/ZFPM2 gene are associated with anomalies of human testis determination.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      the failure of testis development in these cases could be explained by the impaired ability of the
      mutant FOG2 proteins to interact with a known regulator of early testis development, GATA4.
    explanation: >-
      The original small-case functional result supports candidate involvement. The later paper identifies
      which original alleles belonged to the partial case and weakens the interpretation of p.Met544Ile.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:31962012
    reference_title: >-
      Analysis of variants in GATA4 and FOG2/ZFPM2 demonstrates benign contribution to 46,XY disorders
      of sex development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: COMPUTATIONAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Reclassification of the ten ZFPM2 variants revealed six missense were considered benign or likely
      benign (p.E30G, p.D98N, p.S210T, p.L335V, p.M544I, p.M703L).
    explanation: Later variant-specific functional reassessment.
environmental: []
histopathology:
- name: Dysgenetic testis with hypoplastic seminiferous tubules
  description: >-
    Partial disease can include dysgenetic testes, streak tissue or regressed gonads. Observed testicular
    abnormalities include reduced tubular diameter, thick basement membranes, irregular tubules, interstitial
    fibrosis, Sertoli-cell-only tubules and reduced germ cells. Histology contributes to diagnosis and
    neoplasia assessment but does not by itself classify every partial versus complete case; small biopsies
    can miss heterogeneous tissue.
  diagnostic: true
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Features of dysgenetic testis noted were reduced tubular diameter, thickened basal membrane, increased
      interstitial stroma, intracapsular growth, irregular shaped tubules, Leydig cell micronodules or
      hyperplasia, Sertoli cell only tubules, reduced germ cell number, absent spermatogenesis, and tubular
      atrophy (Fig.
    explanation: Direct expert histological review of the registry material.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Results may be inaccurate because of biopsy sampling error; gonadal biopsy may harm the future growth
      and development of the gonad.
    explanation: Broader testicular-development guidance warns about sampling and potential harm.
- name: Gonadoblastoma and germ cell neoplasia in situ in dysgenetic gonads
  description: >-
    Gonadoblastoma and germ cell neoplasia in situ are distinct lesions reported in partial gonadal dysgenesis.
    DHH-related partial disease included GCNIS with incipient stromal invasion and gonadoblastoma. These
    are pathological findings, not an obligatory sequential progression in every gonad.
  diagnostic: false
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25927242
    reference_title: >-
      46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis due to a Homozygous Mutation in Desert Hedgehog (DHH) Identified by Exome
      Sequencing.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: At another site a gonadoblastoma with Call Exner bodies was seen.
    explanation: Direct DHH-case pathology.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      The common types of tumors in all 3 groups were gonadoblastoma (47.8%, n = 32/67), dysgerminoma/seminoma
      (28.4%, n = 19/67), and germ cell neoplasia in situ (11.9%, n = 8/67).
    explanation: Lists the lesion classes across the GD cohort; subgroup counts are in Table 6.
imaging_findings:
- name: Variable or absent Müllerian structures
  modality: MRI
  diagnostic: false
  description: >-
    Ultrasound and, when needed, MRI characterize Müllerian anatomy and gonadal position. A small unestrogenized
    uterus can be missed; discordant imaging requires clinical interpretation. In the cited NR5A1 case,
    ultrasound suggested a primordial uterus while MRI reported absence, so this case does not establish
    definite uterine retention.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38206718
    reference_title: 'NR5A1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: A case report and literature review.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed absence of uterus and ovaries.
    explanation: >-
      In this partial case MRI reported no uterus while ultrasound in the same workup reported a probable
      primordial uterus, so modalities can disagree on small Müllerian remnants and a single negative
      study should not be read as proof of regression.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:38206718
    reference_title: 'NR5A1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: A case report and literature review.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: hypoechoic mass (considered primordial uterus) in posterior bladder
    explanation: >-
      Ultrasound suggested a primordial uterus, while MRI in the same case reported absence. This is suspected,
      discordant anatomy rather than confirmed uterine retention.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:35353710
    reference_title: >-
      Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary
      or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Ultrasound or MRI should be performed to identify a uterus or Müllerian structures; however, a small
      uterus before oestrogen exposure may be missed by imagery.
    explanation: Guideline limitation relevant to anatomy assessment.
- name: Inguinal or intra-abdominal dysgenetic gonads
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  diagnostic: false
  description: >-
    Gonads may be inguinal or intra-abdominal. Localization informs clinical and surgical planning, but
    imaging alone does not establish functional capacity or exclude neoplasia. The registry association
    between labioscrotal location and spontaneous puberty does not demonstrate that repositioning prevents
    tumors.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38206718
    reference_title: 'NR5A1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: A case report and literature review.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The abdominopelvic ultrasound revealed bilateral testicle in bilateral groin.
    explanation: Directly documents inguinal gonads on ultrasound.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
diagnosis:
- name: Integrated clinical, endocrine, and karyotypic assessment
  description: >-
    Integrate genital anatomy, gonadal palpability, family history, associated renal or neurological findings,
    karyotype, and age-appropriate endocrine testing. Assess FSH, LH, testosterone, AMH and often inhibin
    B in clinical context. A blood 46,XY result distinguishes many chromosomal diagnoses but cannot exclude
    low-level or gonad-confined mosaicism.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: clinical assessment
    term:
      id: NCIT:C124351
      label: Clinical Evaluation
  results: Atypical genitalia with a 46,XY karyotype and biochemical evidence of partial gonadal function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36424806
    reference_title: 'Diagnostic approach in 46, XY DSD: an endocrine society of bengal (ESB) consensus statement.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: We recommend formal Karyotyping, even if Y chromosome material has been detected by other methods.
    explanation: Supports formal karyotyping as part of the 46,XY DSD workup.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
- name: hCG stimulation test for residual Leydig-cell function
  description: >-
    hCG stimulation assesses residual testicular testosterone production and can complement the steroid
    profile. It is not a validated stand-alone predictor of spontaneous puberty: the small registry subgroup
    association had P=.087. Endocrine testing cannot identify which gonad functions or determine whether
    both do.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: diagnostic procedure
    term:
      id: NCIT:C18020
      label: Diagnostic Procedure
  results: A preserved testosterone rise indicates functionally significant residual testicular tissue.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Also, a higher proportion of individuals in the spontaneous puberty group had a testosterone response
      to hCG more than double the basal level (88%; n = 15/17, vs 33%; n = 1/3, P = .087).
    explanation: The full-text counts and P=.087 qualify the stronger abstract wording; not validated prediction.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/

    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: Hormonal evaluation cannot distinguish between one versus two functioning gonads.

- name: Broad molecular testing including WT1
  description: >-
    Select molecular testing according to phenotype and family history, using chromosome/CNV assessment,
    a DSD panel, or exome/genome analysis as appropriate. Include clinically relevant genes such as NR5A1,
    MAP3K1, WT1, DHH and DHX37. A pathogenic WT1 finding changes renal and tumor surveillance. A negative
    test does not exclude PGD, and a VUS does not establish a molecular diagnosis. Historical registry
    yield varied by testing method and subgroup.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: genetic testing
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15709
      label: Genetic Testing
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25613702
    reference_title: >-
      WT1 deletion leading to severe 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis, Wilms tumor and gonadoblastoma: case report.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      even in the absence of renal abnormality, it is recommended to test promptly for WT1 defects in
      46,XY gonadal dysgenesis.
    explanation: Directly supports prompt WT1 testing regardless of renal findings.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:36424806
    reference_title: 'Diagnostic approach in 46, XY DSD: an endocrine society of bengal (ESB) consensus statement.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Genetic studies, which include copy number variation (CNV) or molecular testing of a candidate gene
      or next generation sequencing then should be ordered in a stepwise manner
    explanation: Supports the stepwise molecular strategy.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
  - reference: PMID:32352694
    reference_title: WT1 Disorder.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      The diagnosis of WT1 disorder is established in a proband with suggestive clinical findings and

    explanation: >-
      Supplies the GeneReviews diagnostic criterion for the WT1 subtype: molecular confirmation, not clinical
      impression, establishes it.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
  - reference: PMID:40208111

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

      Genetic screening was performed in 78.7% of the cohort with various methods; targeted gene screening
      (71%), gene panels (13%), and whole exome sequencing (15%).
    explanation: Documents heterogeneous methods rather than a mandatory sequential algorithm.
- name: Selective gonadal histopathology and neoplasia assessment
  description: >-
    When gonadal tissue is obtained for a justified clinical indication, expert pathology can characterize
    dysgenesis, germ-cell maturation and neoplasia. Biopsy is subject to sampling error and potential
    harm. Gonadectomy or whole-gonad histology is not required in every patient solely to establish the
    partial phenotype.

differential_diagnoses:
- name: 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis
  description: >-
    Typical complete gonadal dysgenesis presents with female external genitalia, Müllerian structures
    and gonadal failure. Streak gonads are common, but dysgenetic testicular tissue can also occur. Partial
    disease shows more variable anatomy and residual function. Classification integrates phenotype, hormones,
    histology and genetics; tumors can themselves produce sex steroids in either group.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis
    term:
      id: MONDO:0010765
      label: 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Gonadal pre-/malignancy was found in 33.8% in CGD, 19.7% in PGDf, and 8.8% in PGDm.
    explanation: A single cohort scoring both entities documents the tumor-risk gradient that separates them.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:28504475
    reference_title: 'MAP3K1-related gonadal dysgenesis: Six new cases and review of the literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Three of these individuals presented with complete gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by bilateral
      streak gonads with typical internal and external female genitalia, while the other three presented
      with partial gonadal dysgenesis, characterized by incomplete testicular development
    explanation: >-
      Directly contrasts the two phenotypes within one gene's spectrum — the cleanest available statement
      of the distinction.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: 45,X/46,XY mixed gonadal dysgenesis
  description: >-
    45,X/46,XY mosaicism can resemble 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis. Gonadal asymmetry does not distinguish
    them, because a dysgenetic testis and contralateral streak tissue can also occur in 46,XY PGD. Adequate
    chromosome assessment is required, while low-level or tissue-confined mosaicism may escape a blood
    test.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34070473
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant Germ Cell Tumors and Their Precursor Gonadal Lesions in Patients with XY-DSD: A Case Series
      and Review of the Literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: sex chromosome DSD (Klinefelter or Turner Syndrome, chimerism), XX-DSD, and 46 XY-DSD
    explanation: >-
      Supports separation of sex-chromosome DSD from 46,XY DSD; the asymmetric gonadal detail is clinical
      synthesis.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
- name: Partial androgen insensitivity syndrome
  description: >-
    Androgen insensitivity can produce overlapping external genital findings despite testicular differentiation
    and androgen production. AMH, testosterone and hCG responses may overlap with other DSD diagnoses,
    so no single normal hormone result excludes PGD or proves PAIS. Molecular findings and the overall
    anatomical/endocrine pattern guide differentiation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31745530
    reference_title: >-
      Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals Novel Genetic Variants (SRY, DMRT1, NR5A1, DHH, DHX37) in Adults
      With 46,XY DSD.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      partially virilized 46,XY DSD (pvDSD) (n = 25), a group that included partial gonadal dysgenesis
      and those with a broad "partial androgen insensitivity syndrome" label.
    explanation: >-
      Directly documents the clinical conflation of partial gonadal dysgenesis with PAIS, motivating molecular
      resolution.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: 46,XY androgen synthesis disorders
  description: >-
    Steroid synthesis or metabolism defects, including 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 and 5-alpha-reductase
    2 deficiencies, can impair virilization despite testicular differentiation. Steroid profiles, selected
    stimulation testing and molecular results help distinguish these from gonadal dysgenesis; preserved
    AMH alone is not a definitive discriminator.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34070473
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant Germ Cell Tumors and Their Precursor Gonadal Lesions in Patients with XY-DSD: A Case Series
      and Review of the Literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: 46 XY-DSD (disorders of testicular development and disorders of androgen synthesis or action)
    explanation: Supports the mechanistic distinction within 46,XY DSD.
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
- name: Ovotesticular disorder of sex development
  description: >-
    Ovotesticular DSD is defined by ovarian follicular and testicular tissue in the same individual. Histology
    can identify these components when tissue is clinically obtained, but sampling can miss heterogeneous
    tissue. This distinction does not justify routine whole-gonad removal solely for diagnosis.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38206718
    reference_title: 'NR5A1-related 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis: A case report and literature review.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: primary ovarian insufficiency and ovotesticular DSD in 46, XX individuals.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes ovotesticular DSD as a distinct entity within the same gene's phenotypic spectrum; the
      histological criterion is clinical synthesis.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: Testicular regression syndrome
  description: >-
    Testicular regression reflects loss of previously differentiated testicular tissue rather than failure
    to differentiate it. The distinction can be genuinely difficult, and DHX37 variants are found in both
    cohorts, so the two are best regarded as adjacent points on a spectrum of testis-development failure.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: including complete and partial GD (PGD) and testicular regression syndrome (TRS)
    explanation: >-
      Places testicular regression syndrome alongside partial dysgenesis in the same disease group with
      shared genetic causes.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
treatments:
- name: Individualized gonadal management (retention versus gonadectomy)
  action_category: THERAPEUTIC
  description: >-
    Discuss gonadal function, genotype, tissue location, available pathology, age, fertility potential
    and the individual's goals with an experienced DSD team. Nonfunctional high-risk dysgenetic gonads
    may warrant removal; potentially functional gonads may be retained after individualized discussion.
    Sex assignment and a preserved hCG response are not stand-alone indications for removal or retention.
    Surveillance options exist, but no strategy reliably excludes neoplasia; the registry percentages
    are selected histology prevalences rather than prospective risks for retained gonads.

- name: Individualized sex-steroid replacement
  action_category: THERAPEUTIC
  description: >-
    Replace sex steroids when gonadal production is insufficient or after gonadectomy, according to the
    individual's desired pubertal development and clinical needs. Testosterone or 17-beta-estradiol is
    introduced gradually with monitoring; an endometrium-bearing uterus requires addition of progestogen
    after appropriate estrogen priming. Spontaneous pubertal onset does not guarantee completion. Endo-ERN
    guidance supports individualized induction around age 11 for girls with confirmed hypogonadism and
    around age 12 for boys at high risk without pubertal onset. These recommendations cover broader congenital
    hypogonadism; the guideline found no eligible comparative puberty-treatment studies specifically in
    males with PGD.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Hormone Replacement Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15599
      label: Hormone Replacement Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: 17beta-estradiol
      term:
        id: CHEBI:16469
        label: 17beta-estradiol
    - preferred_term: testosterone
      term:
        id: CHEBI:17347
        label: testosterone
  target_phenotypes:
  - preferred_term: Delayed puberty
    term:
      id: HP:0000823
      label: Delayed puberty
  - preferred_term: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
    term:
      id: HP:0000815
      label: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35353710
    reference_title: >-
      Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary
      or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: We recommend to use 17β-oestradiol for puberty induction or to sustain puberty in girls
    explanation: General congenital hypogonadism recommendation, applied with individualized DSD assessment.

      or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline.

      dysgenesis.
    explanation: Explicit evidence limitation from the guideline systematic review.
  target_mechanisms:

    description: >-

      lesion.

- name: Genital reconstructive surgery
  action_category: THERAPEUTIC
  description: >-
    Consider hypospadias repair, orchiopexy or other genital procedures for individualized functional
    goals after multidisciplinary discussion with the patient and family. Decisions should consider timing,
    potential adverse effects, fertility and future autonomy. Moving a functional gonad into the scrotum
    can facilitate examination; it has not been shown here to eliminate tumor risk. GeneReviews notes
    no controlled comparisons of surgical techniques and no consensus on timing.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: orchiopexy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C111066
      label: Orchiopexy
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: surgical options may include hypospadias repair, orchiopexy, scrotoplasty, and phalloplasty.
    explanation: Lists options in broader testicular-development disorders rather than mandatory procedures.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: There is no consensus on the appropriate timing of the surgical procedures listed.
    explanation: Defines the limitation on timing recommendations.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      If a dysgenetic gonad is located in the inguinal canal, it may be placed into the scrotum if results
      indicate some testicular function.
    explanation: Function-dependent option; surveillance remains necessary.
- name: Renal surveillance and Wilms tumor monitoring
  action_category: MONITORING
  description: >-
    For pathogenic WT1-related disease, follow GeneReviews surveillance for proteinuria every six months
    until age ten and annually thereafter, and abdominal ultrasound for Wilms tumor every three months
    until age seven. Follow established renal disease with nephrology. Consider renin-angiotensin system
    inhibition for proteinuria; immunosuppression is ineffective and potentially toxic in WT1-associated
    glomerulopathy. Gonadal management and pubertal monitoring remain coordinated with the DSD team.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: supportive care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK556455/
    reference_title: WT1 Disorder - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Monitor for first appearance of the following: proteinuria every six months until age ten years,
      yearly thereafter; Wilms tumor every three months until age seven years; early gonadal insufficiency
      yearly after puberty.
    explanation: Genotype-specific surveillance from the complete GeneReviews chapter.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK556455/
    reference_title: WT1 Disorder - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: Avoid immunosuppressants, which are ineffective &#x00026; potentially toxic.
    explanation: Applies specifically to WT1-associated glomerulopathy.
- name: Long-term endocrine, growth, and developmental follow-up
  action_category: MONITORING
  description: >-
    Continue endocrine review through puberty and adulthood, including clinical pubertal progression and
    age-appropriate gonadotropins and sex steroids. During induction, guideline follow-up is generally
    every three to six months, with assessment of growth, skeletal maturation, treatment response and
    adverse effects. Spontaneous onset or normal growth in a small series does not guarantee lasting gonadal
    function. Address learning or developmental concerns when present without treating a small-cohort
    observation as a universal PGD feature.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: supportive care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35353710
    reference_title: >-
      Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary
      or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Regular clinical follow-up is generally performed every 3–6 months to assess the effectiveness of
      testosterone therapy by assessing pubertal and skeletal maturation and height velocity.
    explanation: General induction monitoring, not a PGD-specific trial.
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      The patient developed normal puberty at 12 years old but presented with low testosterone levels
      at 17 years old.
    explanation: Direct evidence that endocrine needs may change after spontaneous onset.
- name: Gene-specific genetic counseling
  action_category: COUNSELING_INFORMATIONAL
  description: >-
    Use the established molecular diagnosis and parental testing for recurrence counseling. Autosomal
    dominant allele transmission is distinct from phenotypic penetrance; the <50% estimate in one NR5A1
    family must not be generalized. Counsel NR5A1 relatives about variable gonadal function and primary
    ovarian insufficiency in some 46,XX carriers, WT1 relatives about renal/tumor surveillance, and DHH
    families about recessive inheritance and possible neuropathy. DHX37/NR5A1 dual findings that include
    a VUS or likely-benign allele do not establish digenic recurrence risk. Prenatal or preimplantation
    testing may be discussed when a familial pathogenic variant is known.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Genetic Counseling
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15240
      label: Genetic Counseling
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/316657/5/Laan_Maintext_final.pdf
    reference_title: https://dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/316657/5/Laan_Maintext_final.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Segregation analysis across three generations showed incomplete penetrance (<50%) and phenotypic
      variability among the carriers of NR5A1 c.991-1G>C.
    explanation: Supports family-specific variable penetrance.
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Secondly, patient 3 also carries a loss-of-function variant in NR5A1, which could fully explain
      the PGD phenotype, making the p.Val999Met variant a chance finding.
    explanation: Explains why uncertain dual findings cannot define a recurrence model.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Once the genetic cause of a nonsyndromic disorder of testicular development has been identified
      in an affected family member, prenatal and ... for a pregnancy at increased risk are possible.
    explanation: GeneReviews counseling options for a known molecular diagnosis.
- name: Psychosocial support and shared decision-making
  action_category: COUNSELING_INFORMATIONAL
  description: >-
    Provide developmentally appropriate disclosure, psychological and peer support, sexual-health information
    and fertility counseling. Assigned sex may not match gender identity as it develops. Patients and
    families should participate in decisions, with increasing patient autonomy and careful consideration
    before irreversible interventions. Fertility assessment may include semen testing when appropriate;
    pregnancy options depend on anatomy, gonadal function and the individual's goals.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: supportive care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Open communication with affected individuals and families, including their active participation
      in the decision-making process, is critical.
    explanation: Central shared-decision recommendation.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Assigned sex of rearing may not be congruent with gender identity, which is determined by the individual
      over time.
    explanation: Supports individualized, revisitable goals of care.
- name: Puberty suppression when endogenous puberty conflicts with individual goals
  description: >-
    For selected individuals with functioning retained gonads, hormonal suppression with the desired sex-steroid
    replacement may defer gonadectomy while decisions mature. Two virilizing PGDf individuals in the registry
    received a GnRH analogue, without comparative outcome evidence. Estrogen alone should not be described
    as proven suppression of endogenous androgen effects.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Hormone Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15445
      label: Hormone Therapy
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1547/
    reference_title: Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      If contrasexual puberty occurs, hormonal suppression with replacement of the desired sex hormone
      can be used to avoid gonadectomy until the individual is of age of consent.
    explanation: Broader DSD care option; terminology quoted verbatim from the chapter.
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Two individuals with virilization were treated with a GnRH analogue.
    explanation: Documents use in partial disease without proving comparative efficacy.

discussions:
- discussion_id: gap_xy_pgd_gonad_retention_risk_benefit
  prompt: >-
    What is the prospective, age-specific neoplasia risk in retained gonads in 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis,
    and how reliably can monitoring detect clinically significant lesions?
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  rationale: >-
    Registry estimates arise from selected histology subsets with different gonadectomy ages and inconsistent
    monitoring, not person-time follow-up of all retained gonads. Neither gonadal position nor hCG responsiveness
    is a validated rule for safe retention. Endocrine value and patient goals must be weighed against
    uncertain neoplasia risk.
  attaches_to:
  - treatments#Individualized gonadal management (retention versus gonadectomy)
  proposed_experiments:
  - experiment_id: exp_xy_pgd_retained_gonad_incidence
    name: Prospective registry follow-up of retained gonads in 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis
    description: >-
      Follow retained gonads prospectively within a multinational DSD registry using protocolized imaging,
      tumor markers, and (where performed) biopsy, reporting neoplasia incidence per gonad-year stratified
      by gonadal position and hCG-stimulated testosterone response, rather than prevalence at gonadectomy.
  - experiment_id: exp_xy_pgd_ihc_germ_cell_marker_triage
    name: Immunohistochemical germ-cell marker triage of gonadal biopsy material
    description: >-
      Evaluate whether immunohistochemical germ-cell markers (for example OCT3/4, TSPY, SALL4) on gonadal
      biopsy material can stratify premalignant risk well enough to serve as a triage test for gonad retention
      versus removal.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      However, there was significant variation in monitoring practice amongst centers and only one third
      (n = 34/92) of individuals with PGDm had histology assessment.
    explanation: Primary study identifies ascertainment and surveillance limitations.
- discussion_id: gap_xy_pgd_molecular_yield
  prompt: >-
    Which unsolved partial-gonadal-dysgenesis cases are explained by noncoding variants, tissue-confined
    mosaicism, additional genes or true multilocus effects?
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  rationale: >-
    The I-DSD study identified a likely gene or chromosome alteration in 131/310 across complete and partial
    disease, but only 78.7% underwent screening and methods and variant classification varied. This is
    not evidence of a fixed diagnostic-yield plateau. SOX9 regulatory architecture is relevant broader
    DSD biology; the cited enhancer paper does not establish every deletion as partial disease. The NR5A1/DHX37
    dual-variant cases include uncertain or likely-benign DHX37 findings and do not prove a multilocus
    explanation.
  attaches_to:
  - diagnosis#Broad molecular testing including WT1
  proposed_experiments:
  - experiment_id: exp_xy_pgd_enhancer_genome_sequencing
    name: Genome sequencing with targeted gonadal-enhancer interrogation
    description: >-
      Apply genome sequencing to exome-negative partial-dysgenesis cases with explicit interrogation of
      known gonadal enhancer regions, including the testis-specific enhancers upstream of SOX9, to test
      whether non-coding regulatory variation explains part of the diagnostic gap.
  - experiment_id: exp_xy_pgd_gonadal_mosaicism_sequencing
    name: Deep sequencing of gonadal tissue for gonad-confined mosaicism
    description: >-
      Deep-sequence gonadal tissue obtained at gonadectomy alongside matched blood to test whether mosaic
      variants confined to the gonad account for cases undiagnosed on peripheral-blood testing.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40208111
    reference_title: >-
      Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Genetic screening was performed in 78.7% of the cohort with various methods; targeted gene screening
      (71%), gene panels (13%), and whole exome sequencing (15%).
    explanation: Defines testing ascertainment.
  - reference: PMID:37240737
    reference_title: DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Secondly, patient 3 also carries a loss-of-function variant in NR5A1, which could fully explain
      the PGD phenotype, making the p.Val999Met variant a chance finding.
    explanation: Explicit uncertainty about a dual-variant interpretation.
  - reference: PMID:30552336
    reference_title: Human sex reversal is caused by duplication or deletion of core enhancers upstream of SOX9.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    snippet: Here, we identified four DSD patients with overlapping duplications or deletions upstream of SOX9.
    explanation: >-
      Broader human SOX9 enhancer biology motivates a noncoding hypothesis, without asserting partial-specific
      clinical causation.
- discussion_id: mismatch_xy_pgd_nr5a1_mouse_model_divergence
  prompt: >-
    Do mouse Nr5a1 models faithfully reproduce the human NR5A1 gonadal phenotype, given that the same
    p.R92W substitution induces testicular development in human 46,XX gonads but produces no masculinization
    in XX mice?
  kind: HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH
  status: OPEN
  rationale: >-
    The p.Arg92Trp comparison showed species differences, including absence of XX masculinization in mice
    despite human 46,XX testicular development. This is a caution about translating allele-specific sex-development
    models, not a claim that the mouse directly models every human PGD presentation.
  attaches_to:
  - pathophysiology#NR5A1 sequence alteration
  proposed_experiments:
  - experiment_id: exp_xy_pgd_human_gonadal_organoid_nr5a1_dosage
    name: Human gonadal organoid or iPSC titration of NR5A1 dosage
    description: >-
      Titrate NR5A1 dosage and introduce patient-specific alleles in human-derived gonadal somatic cell
      models (iPSC-derived or fetal gonadal organoid) to establish the human-specific dose-response threshold
      that separates partial from complete testis-determination failure, and compare it directly against
      the corresponding murine threshold.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27833742
    reference_title: >-
      The p.R92W variant of NR5A1/Nr5a1 induces testicular development of 46,XX gonads in humans, but
      not in mice: phenotypic comparison of human patients and mutation-induced mice.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Importantly, mutation-positive XX mice showed no signs of masculinization.
    explanation: >-
      Directly documents the species divergence for the identical allele that masculinizes human 46,XX
      gonads.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- discussion_id: gap_xy_pgd_dhx37_biochemical_mechanism
  prompt: >-
    Do established PGD-associated DHX37 alleles alter RNA-dependent ATPase activity, ribosome maturation,
    or another cell function in developing human gonadal cells?
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  attaches_to:
  - pathophysiology#DHX37 sequence alteration
  rationale: >-
    The original study used structural modeling and expression/localization analysis. Later overexpression
    experiments measured abundance and selected signaling readouts, with unchanged p53 and no increase
    in apoptosis for p.Ser408Leu. The proposed ribosomopathy mechanism and the route from altered protein
    abundance to gonadal differentiation remain unproven.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31337883
    reference_title: >-
      Pathogenic variants in the DEAH-box RNA helicase DHX37 are a frequent cause of 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis
      and 46,XY testicular regression syndrome.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: This raises the possibility that some forms of DSD may be a ribosomopathy.
    explanation: >-
      The authors propose ribosomopathy as a hypothesis in their conclusion; they do not demonstrate variant-dependent
      ribosome dysfunction.
  - reference: PMID:37065748
    reference_title: A novel DEAH-box helicase 37 mutation associated with differences of sex development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Surprisingly, we did not see increases in the p53 protein and cell apoptosis by DHX37 mutation
    explanation: Negative experimental observations constrain the proposed stress mechanism.

notes: "This entry is scoped to the partial phenotype and is deliberately built as the complement of, not a duplicate of, kb/disorders/46_XY_complete_gonadal_dysgenesis.yaml (MONDO:0010765). Where content necessarily overlaps (shared genes, shared tumor substrate), the partial entry emphasizes what is mechanistically different: residual testicular tissue, partial fetal AMH and androgen, ambiguous rather than female genitalia, variable rather than uniform Müllerian retention, potential for spontaneous puberty and for discordant virilization, lower tumor risk, and a genuine gonad-retention trade-off. The gene set overlaps the complete form because most of these genes are dosage-sensitive and produce a spectrum; per-subtype descriptions state which end of the spectrum is being modeled.\nSubtype-scoping decisions, stated explicitly because two of them diverge from the complete-form entry: - NR0B1 and DMRT1 get no subtype here - the partial-specific evidence is thin;\n  they remain in the complete-form entry.\n- SRY and SOX9 get no subtype here, despite being canonical testis-determination\n  genes, because every located citation reports the 46,XY phenotype as complete\n  (sex reversal).\
  \ They are kept as `genetic:` records with that limitation\n  stated. Asserting partial subtypes for them would have meant reusing the\n  complete-form entry's own evidence, which cannot support both.\n- WT1 IS given a subtype here, although the complete-form entry treats syndromic\n  WT1 disease as outside its root. The divergence is deliberate: WT1-related\n  partial dysgenesis is well documented, and the renal/Wilms surveillance and\n  the immunosuppressant warning are management-critical, so the subtype earns\n  its place with its extra-gonadal features scoped to it.\n- ZFPM2 IS given a subtype here, although the complete-form entry declined it on\n  gene-validity grounds. It is retained only as provisional/emerging and is\n  flagged as such in both the subtype and the `genetic:` record; if a\n  gene-validity review rejects ZFPM2, this subtype should go with it.\n\n45,X/46,XY mixed gonadal dysgenesis is out of scope as a sex-chromosome DSD. Frequency bands are given only where a cohort percentage supports them, and the one derived band (ambiguous genitalia) declares its arithmetic.\nKnown gaps for follow-up: no quotable partial-versus-complete AMH or inhibin B comparison was located,\
  \ so those biomarkers are modeled qualitatively rather than with reference values; and an asymmetric streak-plus-testis gonadal pair, though characteristic of this disease, is not curated as a phenotype because no cached source states it quotably. This entry is also a natural member of the Gonadal_Dysgenesis and Digenic_and_Oligogenic_Disorders groupings; adding it there is left as a separate change so this PR stays scoped to one new file."
experimental_models:
- name: MAP3K1 patient lymphoblastoid phosphorylation assays
  description: >-
    Patient lymphoblastoid cell lines carrying selected MAP3K1 alleles were compared with wild-type lines
    after serum starvation and refeeding.
  experimental_model_type: CELL_LINE
  publication: PMID:21129722
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Enhanced MAP3K1-RHOA association
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:21129722
      reference_title: >-
        Mutations in MAP3K1 cause 46,XY disorders of sex development and implicate a common signal transduction
        pathway in human testis determination.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        these mutations altered the phosphorylation of the downstream targets, p38 and ERK1/2, and enhanced
        binding of RHOA to the MAP3K1 complex.

        Patient lymphoblastoid-cell assays support altered MAPK phosphorylation and RHOA association;
        p38 effects differed among alleles.

- name: MAP3K1 p.Arg186Gly overexpression assays
  description: >-
    HEK293T protein-interaction and TCF/LEF reporter assays, with NT2/D1 and KGN phosphorylation/protein-expression
    assays, compared wild type, p.Arg186Gly and relevant empty-vector controls.
  experimental_model_type: CELL_LINE
  publication: PMID:35309143
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Enhanced MAP3K1-RHOA association
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35309143
      reference_title: >-
        MAP3K1 Variant Causes Hyperactivation of Wnt4/β-Catenin/FOXL2 Signaling Contributing to 46,XY
        Disorders/Differences of Sex Development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        Our Co-IP assay confirmed that the binding capacity of MAP3K1R186G to RhoA was 2.57 times that
        of the wild-type protein (Figures 5A,A'), and the ubiquitination degree of the wild-type MAP3K1
        protein was 3.6-fold that of the MAP3K1R186G variant (Figures 5B,B').
      explanation: >-
        Selected p.Arg186Gly variant in HEK293T cells; binding and ubiquitination measurements, not gonadal
        epistasis.

      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        Similarly, in the NT2/D1 testicular cells, phosphorylated p38 and GSK3β proteins were significantly

      evidence_source: IN_VITRO

      snippet: >-
        The data showed that at 48 h after transfection, the relative activity of TCF/LEF in the mutant

- name: DHX37 p.Ser408Leu human Sertoli-cell overexpression
  description: >-

  experimental_model_type: CELL_LINE
  publication: PMID:37065748
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Reduced DHX37 protein abundance
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    evidence:

      reference_title: A novel DEAH-box helicase 37 mutation associated with differences of sex development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        compared with the cells transfected with pcDNA3.1-WT, those with pcDNA3.1-S408L displayed decreased
        DHX37 expression both at the mRNA and protein levels.
      explanation: Variant overexpression effect in a human Sertoli-cell line, with uncertain clinical classification.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37065748
    reference_title: A novel DEAH-box helicase 37 mutation associated with differences of sex development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-

    explanation: Variant overexpression effect in a human Sertoli-cell line, with uncertain clinical classification.
  - reference: PMID:37065748
    reference_title: A novel DEAH-box helicase 37 mutation associated with differences of sex development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      there is no difference in p53 expression among cells transfected with empty expressing vector, wt-DHX37,
      or mutant DHX37.
    explanation: Negative measured result constrains a proposed nucleolar-stress mechanism.
  notes: >-
    The variant had the same localization as wild type. Beta-catenin was higher than in wild-type-transfected
    cells because wild type suppressed it. p53 was unchanged; apoptosis was not increased relative to
    wild-type overexpression, although both constructs increased apoptosis relative to empty vector. Neither
    helicase activity nor ribosome biogenesis was assayed. Clinical pathogenicity remains uncertain.
animal_models:
- name: Sox9-Cre conditional Nr5a1 knockout mice
  species: Mouse
  genotype: Sox9-Cre;Nr5a1flox/flox and Sox9-Cre;Nr5a1flox/-
  publication: PMID:33627800
  description: >-
    Conditional Nr5a1 loss in the Sox9 lineage reduced AMH-positive cells, impaired Sertoli differentiation
    and permitted ectopic FOXL2-positive cells. The reported postnatal spectrum included partial and complete
    gonadal sex reversal.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Incomplete testicular differentiation
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: MODERATE
    limitations: >-
      Lineage-specific engineered biallelic loss is not the same as a human heterozygous NR5A1 allele.
      Leydig-marker reduction differed between the two knockout genotypes. Only the abstract is cached.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33627800
      reference_title: >-
        The conditional deletion of steroidogenic factor 1 (Nr5a1) in Sox9-Cre mice compromises testis
        differentiation.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        These data suggested that the loss of Nr5a1 abrogates the testicular pathway and induces the ectopic
        ovarian pathway, resulting in postnatal partial/complete male-to-female gonadal sex reversal.
      explanation: >-
        Conditional mouse knockout establishes a developmental effect in that model; not a human penetrance
        estimate.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33627800
    reference_title: >-
      The conditional deletion of steroidogenic factor 1 (Nr5a1) in Sox9-Cre mice compromises testis differentiation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM

    explanation: >-
      Conditional mouse knockout establishes a developmental effect in that model; not a human penetrance
      estimate.

Review partial gonadal dysgenesis against full sources; correct clinical denominators and mechanistic overclaims · 2026-09-21T03:49:58Z · View source

Reviewed the complete existing entry and the matching genuine Claude deep-research report. The fresh fully paginated live open-PR search found no overlapping review for this exact disorder, and no prior REVIEW history existed. The disease identity was checked against MONDO/Orphanet before using research leads. Read all 29 originally cited PMID records, distinguishing true main-body text from abstract-only or repository-metadata caches. Regenerated seven PMID caches through just fetch-reference, recovered the Laan primary manuscript and supplementary methods as a canonical repository PDF, and used complete Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development and WT1 Disorder GeneReviews chapters. Additional primary full texts on ZFPM2 reassessment and two DHX37 functional studies were read, together with the Nr5a1 conditional-mouse abstract. Puberty guideline recommendations were checked in context; an independent peer reviewed the applicable Endo-ERN sections. The Laan PDF cache does not expose its main tables, so no new table-only claim was introduced. Corrected the PGD definition to allow variable external anatomy, Müllerian structures and histology. Removed unjustified phenotype frequency bands and pooled arithmetic. Preserved registry denominators for uterus, AMH, inhibin B, puberty and combined neoplasia. The hCG subgroup association was nonsignificant (P=.087), not a validated forecast. Corrected tumor ascertainment, gonadoblastoma-specific versus composite outcomes, neonatal WT1 pathology uncertainty, azoospermia generalization, and imaging discordance. Added direct primary amenorrhea, deep-voice and severe oligozoospermia observations without population extrapolation. Rebuilt the graph as separate genetic perturbations, measured protein interaction/abundance/phosphorylation/transcription events, tissue dysgenesis, developmental hormone inferences and spermatogenic impairment. Retained allele and experimental-system limits. Removed the asserted DHX37 ATPase/ribosome failure and proven digenic model: the dual-variant cases include DHX37 VUS or likely-benign alleles. Corrected ZFPM2 candidacy and predicted rather than measured NR5A1 splice/NMD effects. Did not add a germ-cell-maturation-to-neoplasia edge without evidence of transformation. Five cell models and a conditional mouse model state what they measure and what they cannot establish. Clinical care now distinguishes guideline recommendations from PGD-specific trial evidence, preserves the option of retained functional gonads, acknowledges surveillance limitations, and centers informed patient participation. Added reversible puberty suppression with desired replacement as an option, corrected estrogen-alone anti-virilization claims, and incorporated genotype-specific WT1 surveillance, fertility and family counseling. Removed obligatory whole-gonad histology and rigid molecular-testing sequences. Completeness cross-check: phenotype coverage, supported gene subtypes, atomic mechanisms, care, variant interpretation, diagnosis/biomarkers, citations and overall research consumption were addressed. Environmental testicular-dysgenesis hypotheses, XX animal sex-reversal reports, and general reproductive toxicology do not establish etiologies of this 46,XY PGD entity. Unsolved genetics and DHX37 biochemical mechanism remain explicit knowledge gaps. Peers audited registry rates, DHX37 source classification, clinical/care prose, fetal hormone inference and model limits; all actionable findings were applied. Validation includes authoritative schema, live ontology and exact-cache snippet validation, background/quote-boundary audits, reference and graph gates, and shared-cache consumer checks. Reference cache files were generated only by the sanctioned fetcher; the frozen dataset-accession cache was never read or touched. The standalone tracked PMC fallback is included so two regenerated HTML caches are reproducible; its twelve targeted tests pass. Final verification results and CI are recorded in the PR.

Create: 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis (MONDO:0016674) · 2026-08-01T06:39:18Z · View source

De-novo curation of 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis [MONDO:0016674] fulfilling issue #7595, modelled as CURATE_ROOT_WITH_SUBTYPES. Deep research: "just research-disorder claude_code 46_XY_Partial_Gonadal_Dysgenesis" -- provider claude_code, 20 web searches, 58 turns, 43 citations. Falcon was unavailable in this environment because no EDISON_API_KEY / FUTUREHOUSE_API_KEY is set. The DR report was treated as leads only: every PMID was independently fetched with "just fetch-reference" and every snippet was re-derived as an exact substring of the cached abstract rather than copied from the report, which explicitly warned that its own snippets were page-summarisation paraphrases. GeneReviews baseline: PMID:20301714 -- Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview -- exists but its PubMed abstract is a purpose statement only, so it is tagged in top-level references without inline phenotype evidence. PMID:32352694 -- WT1 Disorder -- is a substantive GeneReviews chapter and supplies the WT1 subtype, the steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and Wilms tumour phenotypes, the surveillance schedule, and the agents-to-avoid warning that the glomerulopathy must not be treated with immunosuppressants. Modelling: the entry is deliberately built as the complement of the existing 46_XY_complete_gonadal_dysgenesis.yaml [MONDO:0010765], which was NOT edited. The organising contrast is residual testicular tissue -- hypoplastic seminiferous tubules rather than fibrous streaks, partial fetal AMH and androgen, ambiguous rather than typically female genitalia, variable rather than uniform Mullerian retention, potential for spontaneous puberty in 80 percent of PGDm with a retained gonad and for discordant pubertal virilization in 42 percent of PGDf with gonads, a lower tumour gradient of 33.8 percent CGD versus 19.7 percent PGDf versus 8.8 percent PGDm in one registry, and a genuine gonad-retention risk/benefit trade-off that does not arise in the complete form. Nine subtypes: NR5A1-related as the characteristic partial gene, MAP3K1-related, SRY-related, WT1-related spanning the Denys-Drash/Frasier continuum, DHH-related with minifascicular neuropathy, DHX37-related, SOX9-regulatory, ZFPM2-related, and Molecularly unresolved. A top-level Digenic inheritance block bound to HP:0010984 captures the documented DHX37 plus NR5A1 double heterozygotes. Three discussions: two KNOWLEDGE_GAP entries covering the retained-gonad tumour-incidence denominator problem and the roughly 50 percent molecularly unexplained fraction, plus one HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH recording that NR5A1 p.R92W masculinises human 46,XX gonads but not XX mice [PMID:27833742]. Validation: just validate, just validate-terms and just validate-references all pass; 156 of 156 snippets verified against cached references; weighted compliance 97.3 percent. All HP, GO, CL, CHEBI, NCIT, HGNC and MONDO terms verified with OAK.

1. Disease Information

1.1 Definition

Orphanet/MONDO definition (verbatim, the source of the MONDO def:):

"46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis (46,XY PGD) is a disorder of sex development (DSD) associated with anomalies in gonadal development that results in genital ambiguity of variable degree ranging from almost female phenotype to almost male phenotype in a patient carrying a male 46,XY karyotype." — Orphanet:251510 (source of MONDO:0016674 definition)

Operational clinical definition. 46,XY PGD is defined by incomplete (rather than absent) testis determination in a person with a non-mosaic 46,XY karyotype and no syndromic features. Gonads are bilaterally dysgenetic testes, or a dysgenetic testis on one side with a streak gonad on the other, and produce enough fetal testosterone and anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) to partially virilize the external genitalia and partially regress the Müllerian ducts — hence the hallmark combination of ambiguous genitalia plus variably retained Müllerian structures.

GeneReviews frames the diagnostic boundary as: "normal general physical examination AND absence of clinical findings involving other organ systems" — i.e., 46,XY PGD in the strict sense is a nonsyndromic disorder of testicular development. Syndromic gonadal dysgenesis (WT1-related Denys–Drash/Frasier, campomelic dysplasia/SOX9, 9p deletion, ATRX, DHH with minifascicular neuropathy) are curated as distinct entities, though they overlap mechanistically. (GeneReviews, Nonsyndromic Disorders of Testicular Development Overview, NCBI Bookshelf NBK1547)

The distinction from CGD is quantitative, not qualitative: PGD retains partial testis-determining function, CGD retains essentially none. The 2025 I-DSD registry study makes this explicit — "46,XY gonadal dysgenesis is classified as complete (CGD) or partial (PGD) subtypes. The phenotype of PGD and the long-term outcome is not clearly defined." (Tadokoro-Cuccaro et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2025; PMID:40208111)

1.3 Synonyms and alternative names

Current/preferred: 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis; 46,XY PGD; 46,XY partial testicular dysgenesis; partial testicular dysgenesis; partial XY gonadal dysgenesis.

Historical/deprecated (do NOT use as preferred terms — explicitly retired by the 2006 Chicago Consensus): male pseudohermaphroditism; partial XY sex reversal; dysgenetic male pseudohermaphroditism; intersex. The Chicago Consensus (Hughes IA, Houk C, Ahmed SF, Lee PA; LWPES/ESPE Consensus Groups. Arch Dis Child 2006;91(7):554-63; PMID:16624884) replaced "intersex, pseudohermaphroditism, hermaphroditism, sex reversal, and gender-based diagnostic labels" with the DSD nomenclature. Note HPO still carries the legacy term HP:0000037 "Male pseudohermaphroditism" — flag it, don't use it.

Terminology sensitivity. Many affected adults and advocacy organisations prefer "differences of sex development" or "variations of sex characteristics" over "disorders." Curated description and notes text should use neutral phrasing; the D/DSD abbreviation is broadly accepted.

1.4 Data provenance character

Information for this entity is overwhelmingly aggregated disease-level and case-series derived, not EHR/individual-patient derived:

  • Registry-derived (highest quality): the I-DSD Registry (international, 34 centres) supplied the only large PGD-specific outcome cohort (n=310 across CGD/PGDf/PGDm; PMID:40208111).
  • National population registry: Danish nationwide cytogenetic/health registry linkage gives the only true population-based prevalence (PMID:27603905).
  • Single-centre case series: Brazilian (São Paulo/Campinas), French (Institut Pasteur), UK, Chinese cohorts — the bulk of the genotype literature.
  • Ontology aggregation: HPO annotations for ORPHA:251510 are curator-derived from Orphanet text, not frequency-counted from patients — treat the "Very frequent"/"Frequent" bands as editorial, not empirical (see §3.1 caveat).
  • No claims-based/OMOP phenotype algorithm exists for 46,XY PGD; ICD coding is too coarse (Q56.3) to support EHR case-finding without chart review or karyotype linkage.

2. Etiology

2.1 Primary causal factors

46,XY PGD is a monogenic (or oligogenic) developmental disorder of testis determination. The proximate cause is a germline (occasionally mosaic) variant that reduces — but does not abolish — the output of the testis-determining gene regulatory network during the narrow window of gonadal fate commitment (human ~gestational weeks 6–8; mouse E10.5–E12.5).

The unifying model, stated by the definitive genetics review:

"In 46,XY men, testis is determined by a genetic network(s) that both promotes testis formation and represses ovarian development. Disruption of this process results in a lack of testis-determination and affected individuals present with 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis (GD), a part of the spectrum of Disorders/Differences of Sex Development/Determination (DSD). A minority of all cases of GD are associated with pathogenic variants in key players of testis-determination, SRY, SOX9, MAP3K1 and NR5A1. However, most of the cases remain unexplained." — Elzaiat M, McElreavey K, Bashamboo A. Genetics of 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;36(1):101633. PMID:35249806

Key etiological points:

  1. Dosage/threshold biology, not simple loss of function. Testis determination is a bistable switch with a steep dose–response. PGD arises when the pro-testis signal falls into an intermediate band — enough to build some seminiferous tubules and Leydig cells, not enough to build a normal testis. This is why the same variant can produce CGD in one family member and PGD (or even isolated hypospadias/infertility) in another.
  2. Both loss-of-function of pro-testis genes and gain-of-function of pro-ovary signalling cause the same phenotype. MAP3K1 is the canonical gain-of-function example (§6.2).
  3. A large diagnostic gap remains. Approximately 50–60% of 46,XY GD cases are genetically unexplained even after exome sequencing (PMID:35249806; Frontiers in Genetics 2024, DOI:10.3389/fgene.2024.1387598). In the largest PGD-specific cohort, "A genetic cause was identified in 42% overall" (PMID:40208111).
  4. Karyotype must be non-mosaic 46,XY. Hidden low-level 45,X/46,XY mosaicism (peripheral blood may be negative while gonadal tissue is mosaic) is a recognised misclassification route into this entity.

2.2 Genetic risk/causal factors

Causal (high-penetrance) loci — see §4 for full detail. Summary of PGD-relevant genes and approximate contribution (GeneReviews NBK1547; PMID:35249806):

Gene Locus Share of nonsyndromic 46,XY testicular DSD Inheritance Direction of effect
NR5A1 (SF-1) 9q33.3 10–15% (up to 42% of PGDf in I-DSD) Sex-limited AD (also de novo; rare AR) LoF / haploinsufficiency
MAP3K1 5q11.2 10–18% (≥4% of PGD+CGD) Sex-limited AD, near-complete penetrance in 46,XY Gain of function
DHX37 12q24.31 ~10–20% (enriched in TRS/PGD) Sex-limited AD Missense, domain-clustered; likely hypomorph
SRY Yp11.2 10–15% (predominantly CGD; PGD when mosaic/partial-function) Y-linked, usually de novo LoF
DHH 12q13.12 Rare AR (sex-limited) LoF
DMRT1 / 9p24 del 9p24.3 Rare AD / contiguous deletion Haploinsufficiency

PPP2R3C, PBX1, HHAT, LHX9, SOS1, MYRF, PPP1R12A, WWOX, TSPYL1, CBX2, ESR2, SART3, AKR1C2/4, ARX, ATRX, MAMLD1 various Individually rare; collectively meaningful mixed mixed

(Gene list compiled from GeneReviews NBK1547; Idris et al., Andrology 2025, PMID:39081229; PMID:35249806)

Y-chromosome microdeletions are NOT a cause of non-mosaic 46,XY PGD. This is a useful negative result: in a Brazilian series of 13 PGD patients, "All STS showed positive amplifications in the PGD group" — no AZF deletions — whereas 6/15 (40%) of the 45,X/46,XY MGD group carried Yq microdeletions (PMC3827999). Curate this as a REFUTE/negative evidence item distinguishing PGD from MGD.

Modifier genes and oligogenicity. A clear genotype–phenotype correlation is absent for NR5A1, which has led to the hypothesis that "genetic modifiers, such as pathogenic variants in other testis/ovarian-determining genes, may contribute to the phenotypic expression." Direct evidence exists: in a 25-patient 46,XY DSD cohort, two patients carried pathogenic variants in both DHX37 and NR5A1, with "the most severe phenotype occurring in the digenic case" — DHX37 p.(Leu467Val) + NR5A1 frameshift, and DHX37 p.(Val999Met) + de novo NR5A1 nonsense (PMC10222664, DHX37 and NR5A1 Variants Identified in Patients with 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis).

Curation flag for this KB: This is a genuine digenic inheritance finding. Per the CLAUDE.md digenic/oligogenic SOP, it warrants an Inheritance block bound to HP:0010984 (Digenic inheritance) with the DHX37+NR5A1 double-heterozygote citation as its own evidence item, and relationship_type: COOPERATING/MODIFIER on the second locus in the genetic: section.

2.3 Environmental risk factors

For 46,XY PGD specifically: essentially none established. This is a genetically determined developmental disorder; no environmental exposure has been shown to cause bona fide 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis with dysgenetic/streak gonads.

Adjacent but distinct — the testicular dysgenesis syndrome (TDS) hypothesis. Skakkebæk and colleagues proposed that cryptorchidism, hypospadias, impaired spermatogenesis and testicular cancer share a common origin in disturbed prenatal testicular development, possibly driven by endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) — anti-androgenic phthalates in particular (Skakkebaek et al., Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2006; PMID:16522521; see also PMID:29183799, "Is testicular dysgenesis syndrome a genetic, endocrine, or environmental disease…?"). Mechanistically, EDCs "may interfere with the control of testicular descent, which is regulated by two Leydig cell hormones, testosterone, and insulin like peptide 3 (INSL3)," and in utero phthalate exposure in rats suppresses fetal-testis steroidogenic gene expression, inducing multinucleated germ cells, hypospadias and cryptorchidism.

How to curate this: TDS is a mechanistically convergent but etiologically separate entity. It shares the downstream node "fetal Leydig cell dysfunction → androgen insufficiency → undervirilization" with PGD, but the trigger is exogenous and the gonad is not dysgenetic in the PGD sense. Record it as a discussion/KNOWLEDGE_GAP or a mechanistic note, not as a risk factor for MONDO:0016674. Most TDS evidence is MODEL_ORGANISM (rat) or ecological-epidemiological; human fetal testis xenografts were notably resistant to phthalate-induced endocrine disruption (PMC3440087) — a genuine human/model mismatch worth recording as HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH.

Other environmental factors: no established role for maternal age, parity, radiation, infection, diet, smoking, or alcohol in 46,XY PGD. Advanced paternal age is a plausible but unquantified contributor to the de novo missense burden (MAP3K1, DHX37, NR5A1) — no PGD-specific study exists. GARD's generic statement that "Environmental factors and viruses may also contribute" is boilerplate text and should not be curated as evidence.

2.4 Protective factors

No genetic or environmental protective factors are established for 46,XY PGD. Two observations that superficially resemble protection but are not:

  1. 46,XX carriers of MAP3K1 and MAP3K1/DHX37 variants are unaffected. "46,XX carriers appear to have normal fertility and no developmental abnormalities." (Ostrer H. Sex Dev 2022; PMID:35290982) This is sex-limited expression, not protection — the same allele is fully penetrant in a 46,XY background.
  2. DHH heterozygotes are asymptomatic (autosomal recessive; GeneReviews NBK1547) — standard recessive carrier status.

gnomAD-based inference: because the causal variants are individually ultra-rare and largely de novo or sex-limited, gnomAD constraint metrics (pLI, missense z) support intolerance rather than identifying protective alleles. No protective haplotype has been reported.

2.5 Gene–environment interaction

No validated GxE interaction for 46,XY PGD. The plausible-but-unproven hypothesis is that sub-threshold germline variants in testis-determining genes (a "genetic first hit" producing borderline SOX9/SF-1 output) may be unmasked by in-utero anti-androgenic exposure, pushing the bistable switch across threshold. This is a specific, testable, currently-unsupported claim — appropriate for a discussions entry with kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP and proposed_experiments (e.g., exposure-stratified genotype analysis in a hypospadias/DSD registry; human fetal-testis organoid dose–response on a sensitized NR5A1+/− background).

3. Phenotypes

3.1 HPO annotation set (ORPHA:251510, retrieved from JAX HPO API; all IDs and labels verified against sqlite:obo:hp via OAK)

Frequency caveat — important for this KB. These frequency bands are Orphanet curator-assigned editorial bands, not counts from a genotyped cohort. Per docs/frequency-evidence-guidelines.md, most of these should be curated without a frequency: value unless a quantitative source is cited. Where a real cohort number exists (I-DSD 2025), I give it separately in §3.2 and that is what should carry the frequency band. The annotation set also clearly pools syndromic causes (nephroblastoma/nephrotic syndrome → WT1; adrenal insufficiency → NR5A1), so the tail annotations describe the gene-defined subgroups, not the core entity.

3.2 PGD-specific quantitative phenotype data — I-DSD Registry 2025 (the best available)

Tadokoro-Cuccaro R, et al. Phenotypic Variation and Pubertal Outcomes in Males and Females With 46,XY Partial Gonadal Dysgenesis. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2025. PMID:40208111; DOI:10.1210/clinem/dgaf223. 310 patients, 34 international centres: CGD n=100, PGD assigned female (PGDf) n=107, PGD assigned male (PGDm) n=103.

These are the numbers that should carry frequency: values in the KB.

Presented with delayed puberty 17.9% (abstract: "18%") — —
